aichi:aioi_unibio.tagline_en: Matcha shochu from a mirin house founded in 1872.
aichi:aioi_unibio.desc_en: Aioi Unibio began in 1872 as a mirin maker in Hekinan, Aichi; in 2004 three companies making mirin, shochu and sake merged into the present firm. It distils shochu carefully by old-style methods, best known for a matcha shochu made with green tea from Nishio, Japan's famous matcha town.

ehime:himebayashi.tagline_en: Japan's first chestnut shochu, from Shikoku's only dedicated shochu kura.
ehime:himebayashi.desc_en: Himebayashi, founded in 1941 in the Shirokawa district of Ehime, is Japan's first maker of chestnut shochu and the only dedicated shochu distillery on Shikoku. Ehime ranks third in Japan for chestnuts, and the house uses 100% local Shirokawa fruit — Okuiyo blends Ehime chestnuts with naked barley, while Okuriokura is pure local chestnut. Distillery tours are possible.

ehime:umebijin.tagline_en: Shochu beside sake, liqueur and gin in the port of Yawatahama.
ehime:umebijin.desc_en: Umebijin Shuzo, founded in 1916 in Yawatahama, Ehime, makes sake, shochu, liqueurs and craft gin — more than 105 years of brewing that leans on local citrus and specialities for its range.

fukuoka:beniotome.tagline_en: The world's first sesame shochu, begun by a 65-year-old founder.
fukuoka:beniotome.desc_en: Beniotome Shuzo was founded in 1978 in Kurume by Haruno Hayashida — then 65 years old — who set out to make a fragrant spirit that could stand beside Western liquor. The result was the world's first sesame shochu. The house distils sesame, barley and sweet-potato shochu with spring water of the Minou mountains, and welcomes visitors at its Minou distillery (9:00–17:00).
features_en: Pioneer of the world's first sesame shochu
Minou mountain spring water; tours open

fukuoka:tenpai.tagline_en: Japan's first 100% barley shochu by atmospheric distillation — nothing added.
fukuoka:tenpai.desc_en: Tenpai, founded in 1898 in Chikuzen, Fukuoka, was the first in Japan to distil a 100% barley shochu by atmospheric distillation. It uses only two-row barley from Fukuoka and Saga, adds nothing at all, and works under the banner of building a distilled spirit Japan can show the world.
features_en: Only Fukuoka and Saga two-row barley, additive-free

fukuoka:kenjou.tagline_en: A patented ginseng shochu and long-aged barley from Tachiarai.
fukuoka:kenjou.desc_en: Kenjou, founded in 1983 in Tachiarai in the Chikugo region, holds a patent for Chin, a shochu made with Korean ginseng grown in the fields along the Chikugo River. Roasted-barley shochu and the long-aged Kiwami Yusha round out an unusually individual range.

fukuoka:asahimatsu.tagline_en: Fune-pressed craft on the headwaters of the Yabe River.
fukuoka:asahimatsu.desc_en: Asahimatsu Shuzo, founded in 1916 in the Kurogi district of Yame, brews and distils with the clear subsoil water of the Yabe River's source and carefully chosen ingredients, holding to traditional fune pressing.

fukuoka:ikekame.tagline_en: Sake, shochu and Japan's first gel umeshu from Mizuma.
fukuoka:ikekame.desc_en: Ikekame Shuzo, in the Mizuma district of Kurume, makes sake, shochu, liqueurs and amazake — and developed Japan's first gel-style umeshu. Its barley shochus include Chikugo Agura and Sasuga.
features_en: Broad range: sake, shochu, liqueur, amazake

fukuoka:goto.tagline_en: Chikugo's oldest kura (1677), ageing shochu in a disused rail tunnel.
fukuoka:goto.desc_en: Goto Shuzojo, founded in 1677 in Yame, is the oldest brewery in the Chikugo district, now in its thirteenth generation. Using subsoil water of the Oku-Yame hills, it makes sake and rice, barley and sweet-potato shochu — including a barley shochu genshu aged over ten years in clay pots inside a tunnel of the old JNR Yabe railway line.
features_en: Pot-aged 10+ years in an old rail tunnel

黒木大藤 古久 10年貯蔵.specs_en: Pot-aged 10+ years in the old Yabe line tunnel

fukuoka:tanoshimaru.tagline_en: Sapporo's barley knowledge distilled — fruit-scented Yawaramugi.
fukuoka:tanoshimaru.desc_en: Tanoshimaru Shuzo was established in 2006 as a production subsidiary of Sapporo Breweries in Kurume. Applying barley expertise honed through beer making, it distils Hokkaido barley with subsoil water of the Minou range (one of Japan's hundred famous waters) into a shochu with a fruity, apple-and-banana nose. It has taken the grand prize twice and gold four times at the Fukuoka Regional Taxation Bureau appraisal.
features_en: Twice grand prize at the Fukuoka appraisal

fukushima:nekka_okuaizu.tagline_en: Rice farmers' domaine shochu from the snow country of Tadami.
fukushima:nekka_okuaizu.desc_en: Okuaizu Distillery was formed in 2016 by a group of local rice farmers in Tadami, deep in the Aizu mountains. Their rice shochu is fully domaine — brewed only from sake rice grown in Tadami — with a stated goal: the world's best rice shochu for Japanese food. It has taken numerous awards, and a tasting room adjoins the distillery (10:00–16:00, paid tastings).

hiroshima:sakurao_bd.tagline_en: A century of distilling behind Hiroshima's long-loved Daruma shochu.
hiroshima:sakurao_bd.desc_en: Founded in 1918 as Chugoku Jozo and renamed in 2021, Sakurao Brewery and Distillery carries more than a century of distilling technique. Its Daruma shochu is a Hiroshima institution and long-seller; the honkaku sweet-potato version is made with Beniazuma potatoes and black koji. Since founding SAKURAO DISTILLERY in 2017 the company also makes gin and whisky, with tours at the visitor centre.
features_en: Gin and whisky at SAKURAO DISTILLERY

hiroshima:miyake_honten.tagline_en: The Sempuku house of Kure — a distiller before it was a sake brewer.
hiroshima:miyake_honten.desc_en: Miyake Honten, founded in 1856 in Kure, actually began with mirin, shochu and shirozake, taking up sake brewing in 1889 under its famous Sempuku name. Shochu has run through the house since its founding, and its SETOUCHI DISTILLERY now distils whisky as well. Bottling-plant tours run by reservation.

hokkaido:godo_shusei_asahikawa.tagline_en: Tantakatan — the red-shiso shochu of Hokkaido, born of a pioneer plant.
hokkaido:godo_shusei_asahikawa.desc_en: The Asahikawa Factory of Godo Shusei was opened in 1900 by Denbee Kamiya, launching Japan's first private-sector industrial alcohol production. Today, as part of the Oenon group, it is best known for Tantakatan, the beloved shiso shochu made with red shiso leaves grown in Shiranuka, Hokkaido.

hyogo:eigashima.tagline_en: Barley shochu inside a 1679 all-rounder of sake, wine and whisky.
hyogo:eigashima.desc_en: Eigashima Shuzo, the Akashi drinks house founded in 1679, brews the sake Kamitaka and makes shochu, wine and whisky. Its distilling history runs deep — a dedicated spirits plant was completed in 1919 for its Shiratama shochu — and today it makes barley shochus such as Yamatodamashii. Tours cover both the sake kura and the whisky distillery.
features_en: Barley shochu in a full-range drinks house

kagoshima:hombo_shuzo.tagline_en: Sakurajima shochu and three distilleries — Hombo's 150-year span.
kagoshima:hombo_shuzo.desc_en: Hombo Shuzo, founded in 1872, is a Kagoshima drinks maker of unusual breadth: honkaku sweet-potato shochu — led by its Sakurajima labels — alongside whisky, wine and liqueurs, with distilleries at Tsunuki, Chiran and Yakushima. More than 130 years of history stand behind the house.
features_en: Distilleries at Tsunuki, Chiran and Yakushima

kagoshima:satsuma_kinzan.tagline_en: Shochu brewed and slept inside the tunnels of a gold mine.
kagoshima:satsuma_kinzan.desc_en: Satsuma Kinzan Kura, part of the Hamada Shuzo group, is the only shochu kura in Kagoshima that ferments, stores and matures inside mine tunnels — the workings of the old Kushikino gold mine. Its Kinzangura is brewed with golden koji. The tunnel brewing halls are open to visitors on weekends and holidays.
features_en: The old Kushikino gold mine reborn

kagoshima:nishi_shuzo.tagline_en: Tomi no Hozan — the shochu that changed how Japan drinks imo.
kagoshima:nishi_shuzo.desc_en: Nishi Shuzo, founded in 1845, brews under the words nature and freedom — rooted in the earth, bound by nothing. Its Tomi no Hozan and Satsuma Hozan carried imo shochu to national fame, and the house now also makes the sake Tenbu and the single malt whisky Ontake, with awards at international competitions. Tours by reservation.
features_en: Tomi no Hozan: a nationally famous imo shochu
Sake Tenbu and whisky Ontake beside the shochu

kagoshima:komasa_jozo.tagline_en: Farm-first shochu, KOMASA GIN and the Kanosuke whisky house.
kagoshima:komasa_jozo.desc_en: Komasa Jozo, founded in 1883, brews to the idea of creating joy together — shochu where the growers' faces are known. Across its two sites, the Hioki Jouryugura and the Kanosuke Distillery, it makes imo shochu led by Satsuma Kozuru, plus KOMASA GIN craft spirits and whisky. Distillery tours are offered.
features_en: KOMASA GIN craft spirits; farm-first sourcing

さつま小鶴.specs_en: Imo shochu, white koji — Koganesengan potatoes

kagoshima:hamada_denbee.tagline_en: Clay pots, wooden stills — Hamada's traditional kura at work.
kagoshima:hamada_denbee.desc_en: Sasshu Hamadaya Denbee is the traditional kura of Hamada Shuzo, founded in 1868. It holds to the old ways at every step — fermentation in clay pots, distillation through wooden stills, maturation again in clay pots — reading the day's weather, temperature and humidity as it goes. Its Den is brewed with yellow koji.

kagoshima:hamada_shuzo.tagline_en: Kaido, DAIYAME and three kura — Hamada's engine room.
kagoshima:hamada_shuzo.desc_en: Hamada Shuzo, founded in 1868, runs three kura — the traditional Denbee Kura, the modern Denzoin Kura and the in-mine Kinzangura — under a declared mission: to make honkaku shochu Japan's true national spirit, and a spirit the world ranks with the best. The Denzoin Kura pairs modern equipment with practised hands for its Kaido and the lychee-scented DAIYAME, whose popularity has surged. Tours at the Denzoin Kura.
features_en: Three-kura system: tradition, innovation and the mine
DAIYAME: a fast-rising modern imo shochu

kagoshima:satsuma_shuzo_ei.tagline_en: The Ei distillery of Satsuma Shuzo, house of Satsuma Shiranami.
kagoshima:satsuma_shuzo_ei.desc_en: The Ei Distillery is one of the production sites of Satsuma Shuzo, the Makurazaki company founded in 1936 whose Satsuma Shiranami led the shochu boom of the 1970s.
features_en: The house that led the 1970s shochu boom

kagoshima:toji_no_sato_kasasa.tagline_en: Keeper of the Kurose toji tradition, with a museum of the craft.
kagoshima:toji_no_sato_kasasa.desc_en: Toji no Sato Kasasa, established in 1992 on the Kasasa coast, carries the legacy of the Kurose toji — the master distillers who once travelled from this district across Kagoshima. A heritage hall at the kura displays the traditional hand-made shochu process, open to visitors.
features_en: Heir to the Kurose toji tradition
Heritage hall showing the hand-made process

kagoshima:satsuma_shuzo_hinokami.tagline_en: Satsuma Shuzo's Hinokami site in Makurazaki.
kagoshima:satsuma_shuzo_hinokami.desc_en: The Hinokami Distillery is a production site of Satsuma Shuzo in Makurazaki, supporting the Satsuma Shiranami range and the long-aged barley shochu Kannoko.
features_en: In the bonito port of Makurazaki

kagoshima:satsuma_shuzo.tagline_en: Satsuma Shiranami — the name that lit the 1970s shochu boom.
kagoshima:satsuma_shuzo.desc_en: Satsuma Shuzo, founded in 1936 in Makurazaki, is one of Kagoshima's defining shochu makers. Its Satsuma Shiranami sparked the nationwide shochu boom of the 1970s, and the house balances that heritage with modern releases like MUGEN Shiranami. Its historic Meiji Kura is open to visitors daily 9:00–16:00.

kagoshima:hombo_tsunuki.tagline_en: Shochu and whisky stills together at Hombo's birthplace, with a bar in the old house.
kagoshima:hombo_tsunuki.desc_en: The Tsunuki Distillery of Hombo Shuzo distils both shochu and whisky at the company's founding ground in Tsunuki. The former family residence now houses Hojo, a café and bar where visitors can taste; tours by reservation.
features_en: Shochu and whisky under one roof
Café-bar Hojo in the old residence

kagoshima:hombo_chiran.tagline_en: Hombo's Chiran site, working black koji in tea country.
kagoshima:hombo_chiran.desc_en: The Chiran Distillery is a production site of Hombo Shuzo in Chiran, southern Kagoshima, distilling sweet-potato shochu brewed with black koji.

kagoshima:shiratsuyu_shuzo.tagline_en: Kyoho-era roots (1730) and famous-waters softness in Yamakawa.
kagoshima:shiratsuyu_shuzo.desc_en: Shiratsuyu Shuzo traces its founding to 1730 in the Kyoho era, making it one of Kagoshima's oldest shochu houses. It distils with natural soft water recognised among Japan's famous waters, and moved to its present home in Yamakawa in 1989.

kagoshima:tamura.tagline_en: First fermentation in clay pots more than a century old.
kagoshima:tamura.desc_en: Tamura, founded in the Meiji 30s (circa 1897), is a traditional kura that still runs its first fermentation in clay pots over a hundred years old, brewing imo shochu with black koji and local ingredients. Visits are possible in the production season (9:00–15:00, contact ahead).

kagoshima:ibusuki_shuzo.tagline_en: Five old kura joined at Lake Ikeda, distilling Riemon.
kagoshima:ibusuki_shuzo.desc_en: Ibusuki Shuzo was formed in 1987 when five long-standing local breweries merged. It distils honkaku imo shochu from Koganesengan potatoes and the waters of Lake Ikeda — Kyushu's largest lake — under its Riemon labels, named in the tradition of Maeda Riemon, who is honoured for bringing the sweet potato to Japan.

kagoshima:nakamata_shuzo.tagline_en: Hand-scooped filtration and clay-pot rest, since 1904.
kagoshima:nakamata_shuzo.desc_en: Nakamata Shuzo, with roots in the Edo period and founded formally in 1904, keeps to traditional methods — filtration scooped by hand, maturation in clay pots — chasing a full, rounded umami that comes from the quality of its ingredients.

kagoshima:denen_shuzo.tagline_en: Japan's first cask-aged barley shochu, with a museum at the kura.
kagoshima:denen_shuzo.desc_en: Denen Shuzo, founded in 1890 in the Sendai area, pioneered cask ageing in shochu — it released Japan's first barrel-aged barley shochu — and continues to build its house around long maturation. A museum adjoins the distillery; tours by reservation.
features_en: Long maturation as the house style

kagoshima:murao_shuzo.tagline_en: Murao — one of the fabled 3M shochu, brewed in clay pots.
kagoshima:murao_shuzo.desc_en: Murao Shuzo, founded in 1902, distils by black koji and clay-pot fermentation in the old way. Its Satsuma Chaya takes its name from a Satsuma-domain teahouse that once stood nearby, and Murao itself is one of Japan's most sought-after imo shochus — famously hard to find.

kagoshima:yamamoto_shuzo.tagline_en: Satsuma Godai — a century of Sendai brewing, rested 150 days.
kagoshima:yamamoto_shuzo.desc_en: Yamamoto Shuzo, founded in 1912 in the Sendai area, carries more than a century of history. Its shochus mature over 150 days in single tanks, led by Satsuma Godai and Kura no Kami. Visits are possible with advance contact (8:00–17:00).

kagoshima:izumi_shuzo.tagline_en: Wooden stills and clay pots beside a soba restaurant, in the crane city.
kagoshima:izumi_shuzo.desc_en: Izumi Shuzo, founded in 1950 in Izumi — the winter home of Japan's cranes — pairs modern equipment with traditional tools it refuses to retire, from wooden stills to clay pots. A visitor centre and a soba restaurant adjoin the kura, with tours year-round.
features_en: Wooden stills and clay pots kept in use

kagoshima:unkai_shuzo_izumi.tagline_en: Unkai's Izumi kura — southern Kyushu potatoes, Shibi mountain water.
kagoshima:unkai_shuzo_izumi.desc_en: The Izumi Kura of Unkai Shuzo distils honkaku imo shochu from southern Kyushu sweet potatoes and natural spring water of the Shibi mountains, home of its Satsuma Kobiki label.

kagoshima:nagashima_kenkyo.tagline_en: Five island kura, one blend — Satsuma Shimabijin.
kagoshima:nagashima_kenkyo.desc_en: Nagashima Kenkyo, founded in 1967 on Nagashima Island, blends the base spirits of the island's five distilleries into one balanced, full-flavoured imo shochu — the well-loved Satsuma Shimabijin (Island Beauty) and its black-koji sister.
features_en: A blend of five island kura's spirits

kagoshima:kami_shuzo.tagline_en: Chizuru — brewed in clay pots buried in the earth since 1868.
kagoshima:kami_shuzo.desc_en: Kami Shuzo, founded in 1868, still ferments in clay pots buried in the ground, in the traditional Kagoshima way. With spring water of the Shibi mountains and select sweet potatoes, its Chizuru aims at a deep flavour of fragrant richness and refined sweetness.

kagoshima:oishi_shuzo.tagline_en: Named for the cranes that fly from Siberia to Akune.
kagoshima:oishi_shuzo.desc_en: Oishi Shuzo, founded in the Meiji era (1899), took the name of its Tsurumi label from the cranes its founder watched arriving from Siberia to winter on the Izumi plain. A small house, it produces about 1,000 koku a year.

kagoshima:oguchi_shuzo.tagline_en: Kuro Isanishiki — the black-koji standard of the Isa valley.
kagoshima:oguchi_shuzo.desc_en: Oguchi Shuzo was established in 1970 through the full cooperation of eleven breweries of Isa, the cold northern valley of Kagoshima. Its Kuro Isanishiki stands among the defining black-koji imo shochus, with clay-pot and classic versions beside it.

kagoshima:kai_shoten.tagline_en: Isami — four generations behind one coveted black-koji shochu.
kagoshima:kai_shoten.desc_en: Kai Shoten, founded in 1904 and now in its fourth generation, makes a single famous thing: Isami, a black-koji imo shochu so sought after it is notoriously hard to find.

kagoshima:oyama_shuzo.tagline_en: Isa Daisen — a small kura of the cold Isa valley.
kagoshima:oyama_shuzo.desc_en: Oyama Shuzo, founded in 1905 in Isa, Kagoshima, distils the imo shochu Isa Daisen, with a black-koji BLACK version beside the original.

kagoshima:sato_shuzo.tagline_en: Sato — the white and the black, premium shochu of Kirishima.
kagoshima:sato_shuzo.desc_en: Sato Shuzo, founded in 1906 in the Makizono district of Kirishima, brews the premium imo shochus Sato White (white koji) and Sato Black (black koji) — both nationally famous and famously hard to obtain — holding to traditional methods in the Kirishima hills.
features_en: Sato White and Black: coveted premium shochu

kagoshima:kirishimacho_distillery.tagline_en: Akarui Noson — clay-pot shochu from the Bright Farming Village.
kagoshima:kirishimacho_distillery.desc_en: Kirishimacho Distillery, founded in 1911 at the foot of the Kirishima range, brews traditional Kagoshima shochu in clay pots — its cheerfully named Akarui Noson (Bright Farming Village) leads the range, with red-potato and roasted purple-potato versions beside it. ISO 9001 certified since 2013, the kura is open to visitors year-round (9:00–17:00).

kagoshima:kokubu_shuzo.tagline_en: All-potato shochu and a revived heirloom vine — Kokubu's laboratory.
kagoshima:kokubu_shuzo.desc_en: Kokubu Shuzo brews with local sweet potatoes and rice and water drawn from about 100 metres underground. For more than thirty years toji Nobuhisa Yasuda has pushed at shochu's possibilities — developing an all-potato shochu with koji grown on sweet potato instead of rice, and reviving the heirloom potato variety Tsurunashi Genji.
features_en: Revived the heirloom Tsurunashi Genji potato

いも麹芋.specs_en: All-potato — koji grown on sweet potato

kagoshima:nakamura_shuzojo.tagline_en: Every drop clay-pot brewed and atmospheric-distilled since 1888.
kagoshima:nakamura_shuzojo.desc_en: Nakamura Shuzojo, founded in 1888, has carried its handwork through more than 130 years: every product is fermented in clay pots and distilled at atmospheric pressure, led by the black-koji Gyokuro.

玉露（黒）.specs_en: Imo shochu — black koji, clay-pot brewed

kagoshima:manzen_shuzo.tagline_en: Manzen — hand-made koji and wooden stills deep in the Kirishima forest.
kagoshima:manzen_shuzo.desc_en: Manzen Shuzo stands alone in the mountains of Kirishima National Park, brewing by the full traditional array: hand-made koji, clay-pot fermentation and wooden-still distillation. Its Manzen and Manzen-an are cult favourites among imo shochu lovers.
features_en: Alone in the Kirishima National Park forest
Hand-made koji, clay pots, wooden stills

kagoshima:shirakane_shuzo.tagline_en: Shirakane no Tsuyu and a stone-built museum kura from 1869.
kagoshima:shirakane_shuzo.desc_en: Shirakane Shuzo, founded in 1869 in Aira, is among Kagoshima's oldest shochu houses. Its stone kura now doubles as the Ishigura Museum, open to visitors (10:00–17:00, closed Wednesdays), while the house distils Shirakane no Tsuyu and the stone-kura-brewed Ishigura.
features_en: Stone-built Ishigura Museum at the kura

kagoshima:okubo_shuzo.tagline_en: Samurai no Mon — clay-pot shochu from its own farm's potatoes.
kagoshima:okubo_shuzo.desc_en: Okubo Shuzo, founded in 1910 in the Osumi region, brews in clay pots by traditional method, sourcing its sweet potatoes from an affiliated farm and contract growers. Its Samurai no Mon is the flagship.
features_en: Own affiliated farm and contract growers

kagoshima:tensei_shuzo.tagline_en: Drum-koji precision on the spring water of Fuzendo, since 1901.
kagoshima:tensei_shuzo.desc_en: Tensei Shuzo, founded in 1901 in the Osumi region, runs its own drum-type koji machine under computer control — precision brewing on the natural spring water of Fuzendo. Tours by reservation, best in October and November.

kagoshima:wakashio_shuzo.tagline_en: Two kura, one house — tradition at Sengoku, technology at Shisan.
kagoshima:wakashio_shuzo.desc_en: Wakashio Shuzo, founded in 1968 in Shibushi, brews across two facilities — the traditional Sengoku Kura and the modern Shisan Kura — fusing old technique with current technology in its Satsuma Wakashio white and black and other labels. Tours by reservation.

kagoshima:marunishi_shuzo.tagline_en: Mukashi Mukashi — once upon a time, distilled in Osumi.
kagoshima:marunishi_shuzo.desc_en: Marunishi Shuzo, founded in 1916, has distilled imo shochu on the Osumi Peninsula for over a century at its Futsuhara distillery. Its storybook-named Mukashi Mukashi (Once Upon a Time) leads black- and white-koji companions. Tours by reservation (9:00–17:00).

kagoshima:iwagawa_jozo.tagline_en: Oyattosaa — 'good work today' in Kagoshima dialect, since 1870.
kagoshima:iwagawa_jozo.desc_en: Iwagawa Jozo, founded in 1870 in the Osumi region, balances tradition with modern tastes. Its flagship Oyattosaa takes its name from the Kagoshima dialect greeting for a day's work well done.

kagoshima:shiratama_jozo.tagline_en: Mao — the Demon King, one of the three legendary M's.
kagoshima:shiratama_jozo.desc_en: Shiratama Jozo, founded around 1888 at the southern tip of the Osumi Peninsula, brews Mao — the Demon King — one of the fabled 3M premium shochus alongside Moriizo and Murao. Famed for an apple-like, almost ginjo aroma, it is drunk straight or on the rocks by devotees nationwide; Shiratama no Tsuyu, Genroin and Tenchu complete the range.
features_en: Mao: one of the legendary 3M shochus

kagoshima:moriizo.tagline_en: Moriizo — the first of the 3M, sold only by telephone lottery.
kagoshima:moriizo.desc_en: Moriizo Shuzo, founded in 1885, brews the most storied name in premium imo shochu. Everything is done as it always was: Japanese clay pots only, koji from Kagoshima rice, contract-grown sweet potatoes, careful distillation. Moriizo — first among the legendary 3M with Mao and Murao — is sold only through a telephone lottery, never online, with a JAL international in-flight allocation its other famous channel.
features_en: Sold only by telephone lottery — never online

kagoshima:taikai_shuzo.tagline_en: The biggest hand-made kura — thirty brands, temperatures checked by hand.
kagoshima:taikai_shuzo.desc_en: Taikai Shuzo, founded in 1967 in Kanoya, styles itself the largest hand-made kura: fermentation temperatures are still managed by hand, ingredients come through close ties with contract farmers, and a rice traceability system tracks the koji grain. More than thirty shochu brands carry its concept of tradition and challenge. Tours are accepted.

kagoshima:mitake_shuzo.tagline_en: Mitake — the shochu of Yakushima's World Heritage waters.
kagoshima:mitake_shuzo.desc_en: Mitake Shuzo, founded in 1958 on Yakushima, distils with the abundant waters of the World Natural Heritage island. Its Mitake pairs a clean, crisp finish with the aroma, umami and depth of the sweet potato, with genshu and island-only editions for those who make the crossing.

kagoshima:hombo_yakushima.tagline_en: Clay-pot shochu on Yakushima's soft water — Hombo's heritage kura.
kagoshima:hombo_yakushima.desc_en: The Yakushima Denshogura of Hombo Shuzo distils hand-made shochu in clay pots, working Yakushima's soft island water and fine sweet potatoes into its Yakusugi, named for the island's ancient cedars.

kagoshima:arimura_shuzo.tagline_en: Yoron Island's only kokuto shochu kura — Shimayusen.
kagoshima:arimura_shuzo.desc_en: Arimura Shuzo is the only Amami kokuto (brown sugar) shochu maker on Yoron Island, begun as a distillery in 1947 and licensed in 1959. It brews Shimayusen with white and black koji, Thai rice and island groundwater, at 20 and 35 degrees.
features_en: Yoron Island's only kokuto shochu kura
White and black koji with island groundwater

kagoshima:harada_shuzo.tagline_en: Shoryu — kokuto shochu aged five years and more on Okinoerabu.
kagoshima:harada_shuzo.desc_en: Harada Shuzo, founded in 1947 on Okinoerabu Island, devotes itself to long maturation: its kokuto shochu Shoryu (Rising Dragon) rests five years or more before release.

kagoshima:niiro_shuzo.tagline_en: Tenkaichi — a century of unchanged flavour on Okinoerabu.
kagoshima:niiro_shuzo.desc_en: Niiro Shuzo, established in 1920 on Okinoerabu Island, has kept its kokuto shochu tasting as it did at the founding for over a century. Its Tenkaichi (First Under Heaven) owes its name to words from a doctor close to the fourth-generation head. Tours with tastings by reservation — best in the January–June production season.

kagoshima:okinoerabu_shuzo.tagline_en: Four island kura bottling together since 1969.
kagoshima:okinoerabu_shuzo.desc_en: Okinoerabu Shuzo was established in 1969 as the joint bottling and sales company of four distilleries on Okinoerabu Island, producing Amami kokuto shochu including an aged koshu.
features_en: Joint company of four island kura

kagoshima:kanzaki_sangyo.tagline_en: A small member kura of the Okinoerabu cooperative.
kagoshima:kanzaki_sangyo.desc_en: Kanzaki Sangyo, founded in 1950, is one of the small member distilleries of Okinoerabu Shuzo, contributing spirit to the island's shared kokuto shochu.

kagoshima:sasada_shuzo.desc_en: Sasada Shuzo is a distillery on Okinoerabu Island and one of the member kura of Okinoerabu Shuzo, the island's joint bottling company.

kagoshima:oki_shuzo.desc_en: Oki Shuzo, founded in 1917, is one of the member kura of Okinoerabu Shuzo, holding to small-scale, careful traditional distilling on the island.

kagoshima:amami_nishikawa.tagline_en: Shima no Napoleon — Tokunoshima's first walkable distillery.
kagoshima:amami_nishikawa.desc_en: Amami Oshima Nishikawa Shuzo, founded in 1950 on Tokunoshima, brews the island favourite Shima no Napoleon and Mikado. In 2019 it opened a new plant with the island's first visitor course, where the kokuto shochu process can be seen up close (10:00–16:00, weekdays, by reservation).

kagoshima:amami_shurui.tagline_en: Five Tokunoshima kura in one blend — and island rum besides.
kagoshima:amami_shurui.desc_en: Amami Shurui was established in 1965 as the joint bottling and sales company of five Tokunoshima distilleries — Kamezawa, Amakawa, Takaoka, Nakamura and Matsunaga — blending their spirits into its Amami kokuto shochu. The group also distils Rurikakesu Rum from island sugarcane.

kagoshima:matsunaga_shuzo.tagline_en: A Tokunoshima member kura of the Amami Shurui group.
kagoshima:matsunaga_shuzo.desc_en: Matsunaga Shuzojo is a Tokunoshima distillery and one of the member kura of Amami Shurui, contributing to the shared Amami label alongside its own Marushika.

kagoshima:nakamura_shuzo_amami.tagline_en: Fragrant kokuto spirit for the island's shared label, since 1947.
kagoshima:nakamura_shuzo_amami.desc_en: Nakamura Shuzo, founded in 1947 on Tokunoshima, is a member kura of Amami Shurui, distilling notably aromatic kokuto shochu for the shared Amami brand.

kagoshima:amakawa_shuzo.tagline_en: A founding member of Kagoshima's first joint bottling venture.
kagoshima:amakawa_shuzo.desc_en: Amakawa Shuzo, founded in 1947 on Tokunoshima, is a member kura of Amami Shurui and was among the six houses that established Kagoshima's first joint bottling operation in 1965. Its own label is Amakawa.
features_en: Part of Kagoshima's first joint bottling venture (1965)

kagoshima:takaoka_jozo.tagline_en: Kokuto shochu and Japanese rum from Tokunoshima, since 1949.
kagoshima:takaoka_jozo.desc_en: Takaoka Jozo, founded in 1949 on Tokunoshima, is a member kura of Amami Shurui making the kokuto shochu Bandai — and one of the group's houses behind the Japanese-made Rurikakesu Rum.

kagoshima:kamezawa_shuzo.tagline_en: Atmospheric-distilled spirit for the Amami blend.
kagoshima:kamezawa_shuzo.desc_en: Kamezawa Shuzojo is a Tokunoshima distillery and member kura of Amami Shurui, distilling and storing kokuto shochu at atmospheric pressure for the shared Amami label.

kagoshima:kikaijima_shuzo.tagline_en: Nothing leaves for a year — patient kokuto shochu of Kikai Island.
kagoshima:kikaijima_shuzo.desc_en: Kikaijima Shuzo, founded in 1916 on the coral island of Kikai, holds to atmospheric distillation and a house rule of patience: every product rests at least a year before shipping — three, for its aptly named Sannen Netazo (Three-Year Sleeper).
features_en: All products aged 1+ year before release

kagoshima:asahi_shuzo_amami.tagline_en: Organic sugarcane from its own fields, on the coral island of Kikai.
kagoshima:asahi_shuzo_amami.desc_en: Asahi Shuzo, founded in 1916 on Kikai Island, is devoted to kokuto shochu — the spirit only the Amami islands may make. Since 1999 it has grown its own sugarcane organically, with JAS organic certification, feeding its Asahi and companion labels.
features_en: Own organically grown sugarcane, JAS certified

kagoshima:machida_shuzo.tagline_en: Sato no Akebono — the vacuum-distilled shochu that opened kokuto to everyone.
kagoshima:machida_shuzo.desc_en: Machida Shuzo was the first in the kokuto shochu world to adopt vacuum distillation, in 1990. The result, Sato no Akebono, drank smooth and easy where older kokuto shochu had bite — a breakthrough that reshaped the category, now offered in long-aged and gold editions.
features_en: First vacuum distillation in kokuto shochu (1990)
Sato no Akebono: the smooth pioneer

kagoshima:yamada_shuzo.tagline_en: A family kura growing its own cane for Amami Nagakumo.
kagoshima:yamada_shuzo.desc_en: Yamada Shuzo, founded in 1954, is a family-run kura on Amami Oshima that grows its own sugarcane and rice, working Amami and Okinawan brown sugar into its Amami Nagakumo.
features_en: Grows its own sugarcane and rice

kagoshima:amami_oshima_shuzo.tagline_en: 100% Amami-grown brown sugar, vacuum-distilled to a gentle sweetness.
kagoshima:amami_oshima_shuzo.desc_en: Amami Oshima Shuzo works only with brown sugar grown on Amami Oshima itself, vacuum-distilling it into the smooth, deep-sweet Jogo and Hamachidori. Tours run weekdays at 10:00, 14:00 and 16:00 (weekends by advance contact).

kagoshima:amami_kaiun_densho.tagline_en: The Naze heritage kura of Kaiun Shuzo, brewing Amami Rokucho.
kagoshima:amami_kaiun_densho.desc_en: The Amami Denshogura in Naze, founded in 1950 and carried forward through a 2015 business succession by Amami Oshima Kaiun Shuzo, continues the kokuto shochu tradition with its Amami Rokucho, named for the island's folk dance rhythm. Tours by reservation, November to February.

kagoshima:tomita_shuzojo.tagline_en: Ryugu — clay pots only, in the old suppon style.
kagoshima:tomita_shuzojo.desc_en: Tomita Shuzojo, founded in 1951 in Naze, brews its Ryugu in clay pots alone, keeping the traditional suppon-style fermentation. A small-production house, it distils nearly year-round outside summer and the New Year. Visits by reservation (13:00–17:00).

kagoshima:amami_kaiun.tagline_en: Lento — kokuto shochu matured to music.
kagoshima:amami_kaiun.desc_en: Amami Oshima Kaiun Shuzo brews Lento, named from the musical term for slowly — the kokuto shochu that carried Amami's spirit to the nation. Vacuum distillation gives its easy smoothness, natural water of Mt. Yuwan feeds the mash, and its tanks are played sound vibrations in the company's acoustic maturation method. Beni Sango and FAU widen the range.
features_en: Lento: Amami's defining modern kokuto shochu
Acoustic maturation — sound played into the tanks

kagoshima:nishihira_shuzo.tagline_en: Sango — coral-named kokuto shochu from Naze, since 1927.
kagoshima:nishihira_shuzo.desc_en: Nishihira Shuzo, founded in 1927 and settled at its present Naze site in 1946, distils kokuto shochu by methods handed down through the generations, under its coral-named Sango label.

kagoshima:nishihira_honke.tagline_en: Seventeen straight years of honours at the Kagoshima appraisal.
kagoshima:nishihira_honke.desc_en: Nishihira Honke has taken the excellence award at the Kagoshima honkaku shochu appraisal seventeen years running, crowned by the president's award in 2019. Its Seegore leads a range that includes five-year and cask-aged expressions.

kanagawa:koganei_shuzo.tagline_en: Sake-lees shochu, gin and beer at the foot of the Tanzawa range.
kanagawa:koganei_shuzo.desc_en: Koganei Shuzo, founded in 1818 in the Nanasawa district of Atsugi at the foot of the eastern Tanzawa mountains, brews the local sake Morimasu and ranges wide — honkaku shochu vacuum-distilled from sake lees and rice koji, craft gin, craft beer and junmai hon-mirin.
features_en: Sake-lees shochu, gin, beer and mirin

kochi:mutemuka.tagline_en: Dabada Hiburi — chestnut shochu named for firelit fishing on the Shimanto.
kochi:mutemuka.desc_en: Mutemuka, founded in 1893 in the mountains above the upper Shimanto River, bears a name meaning unadorned and true of heart. Its celebrated chestnut shochu Dabada Hiburi is distilled slowly at low temperature with 50% chestnut — named for hiburi, the traditional fire-swinging ayu fishing of the Shimanto, and daba, the gathering places along its banks. Kura visits are possible in the river valley.
features_en: Named for the Shimanto's fire-fishing tradition

kochi:kikusui_kochi.tagline_en: Chestnut and barley shochu from Aki, with an all-women planning team.
kochi:kikusui_kochi.desc_en: Kikusui Shuzo, established in 1948 in Aki, Kochi, makes chestnut and barley shochu alongside its sake. The barley shochu Ryoma pours clean and gentle — an easy first shochu — and the house runs a product planning team composed entirely of women, developing releases with women drinkers in mind.

kumamoto:takahashi_shuzo.tagline_en: Hakutake and Shiro — the names that carry Kuma shochu to the nation.
kumamoto:takahashi_shuzo.desc_en: Takahashi Shuzo, founded in 1900 in Hitoyoshi, brews Hakutake and Shiro — the defining brands of Kuma shochu, the rice shochu of the Kuma valley. Under its creed of good rice, good water, good people, it runs three production sites — the Taragi distillery, the Hakutake research institute and the Tano whisky distillery in a reborn village school — with capacity of 100,000 koku. The Kuma Shochu Museum Hakutake Denshogura welcomes visitors.
features_en: Hakutake: the flagship name of Kuma shochu

kumamoto:hakutake_kenkyusho.tagline_en: The research kura behind Hakutake's quality, additive-free.
kumamoto:hakutake_kenkyusho.desc_en: The Hakutake Shuzo Research Institute, established in 1986, is Takahashi Shuzo's original shochu plant. Selecting rice and water strictly and using no additives whatsoever, it produces the Hakutake and Shiro that anchor the group's quality.

kumamoto:sengetsu.tagline_en: Six generations of in-house toji behind the Crescent Moon.
kumamoto:sengetsu.desc_en: Sengetsu Shuzo was founded in 1903 by Jisuke, the first master, and has kept its own in-house toji ever since — six generations of them guarding the house technique. Its Sengetsu (Crescent Moon) stands among the flagship names of Kuma shochu, brewed in central Hitoyoshi where the kura welcomes visitors.
features_en: A flagship name of Kuma shochu

kumamoto:fukano.tagline_en: Twenty-year clay-pot koshu from a house begun in 1823.
kumamoto:fukano.desc_en: Fukano Shuzo began in 1823 when its founder Tokiji Fukano moved from Kurume to Hitoyoshi and took up shochu making. Now led by seventh-generation Seiichi Fukano (president since 2015), the house is known for long maturation — including a koshu rested twenty years in clay pots — under labels like Iroha and Homare no Tsuyu.

kumamoto:fusanotsuyu.tagline_en: Casks, pots and bottles — layered maturation in Taragi.
kumamoto:fusanotsuyu.desc_en: Fusanotsuyu, founded in 1907 in Taragi, carries the 500-year Kuma shochu tradition forward with a particular devotion to maturation — resting its spirit in casks, clay pots and bottles to layer depth and hidden complexity. It grows its own sweet potatoes for the imo side of a range centred on rice shochu.
features_en: Maturation across cask, pot and bottle
Own farm for its potato shochu

kumamoto:rokuchoshi.tagline_en: Nothing leaves before its time — twelve years' average rest.
kumamoto:rokuchoshi.desc_en: Rokuchoshi Shuzo, founded in 1923 at the centre of the Kuma basin, is a specialist in aged shochu: its spirit matures an average of twelve years or more before shipping. That patience has earned three-star honours at overseas spirits competitions.

kumamoto:matsunoizumi.tagline_en: Suikyo Mushi — brewed on the moonlight water of Yamizo Yakushi.
kumamoto:matsunoizumi.desc_en: Matsunoizumi Shuzo brews in Asagiri, at the heart of the Kuma valley, since 1875. Its founder Bunsuke Matsuoka chose the site for the famed Gekkosui — moonlight water — filtering through the granite of Mt. Shiraga at the Taniyakushi temple spring. The house brews its Suikyo Mushi with ginjo yeast and special spring-water methods.
features_en: Gekkosui spring water of Mt. Shiraga

kumamoto:tsunematsu.tagline_en: Kuma Ken — named for the valley's hand-game, filtered by hand.
kumamoto:tsunematsu.desc_en: Tsunematsu Shuzo Honten, founded in 1917 in Taragi, brews with natural water rising from a hundred metres underground and Hinohikari rice it grows in the paddies surrounding the kura. It finishes without machine filtration, by hand — its Kuma Ken takes the name of the valley's famous drinking hand-game.
features_en: Water from 100m down; rice from its own paddies

kumamoto:ohishi.tagline_en: Amber rice shochu — fifty years of cask ageing at the Kuma's source.
kumamoto:ohishi.desc_en: Oishi Shuzojo, founded in 1872 in Mizukami at the uppermost reach of the Kuma River, brews under fifth-generation head Choichiro Oishi at the foot of sacred Mt. Ichifusa. The house began cask ageing some fifty years ago — long before it was fashionable — and its amber, long-rested rice shochus now sit beside rice-shochu liqueurs and whisky.
features_en: At the source of the Kuma River
Whisky and liqueurs beside the shochu

kumamoto:torikai.tagline_en: Ginka Torikai — the first shochu with a ginjo nose, and the house's only bottle.
kumamoto:torikai.desc_en: Torikai Shuzo has kept a kura in the Nanokamachi quarter of Hitoyoshi for more than four hundred years. In 1994 it achieved something unprecedented: Ginka Torikai, the first honkaku shochu with a true ginjo aroma. The house sells that one product and nothing else — quality distilled to a single answer.

吟香鳥飼.specs_en: Ginjo-aroma rice shochu — the house's sole product

kumamoto:toyonaga.tagline_en: Organic Kuma rice from its own paddies, poured in twelve countries.
kumamoto:toyonaga.desc_en: Toyonaga Shuzo was founded in 1894 in Yunomae by Tsurumatsu Toyonaga. Fourth-generation head Shiro Toyonaga brews to a strict local creed — Kuma rice, Kuma water, Kuma people — with organic Kuma rice from the house's own fields at the centre of its Toyonaga Kura label. Gold medals at the Los Angeles International Spirits Competition have helped carry it to twelve countries.
features_en: Organic rice from its own paddies

kumamoto:joraku.tagline_en: Oak and sherry casks in the Kuma valley, since 1912.
kumamoto:joraku.desc_en: Joraku Shuzo, founded in 1912 in Mizukami and relocated to Nishiki in 1994, matures its shochu spirit long in casks chosen for their wood — oak and sherry among them, rested 24 months and more. Local Nishiki fruit liqueurs and a yogurt shochu stretch the range beyond the Kuma tradition.
features_en: Oak and sherry cask maturation, 24+ months
Fruit liqueurs and yogurt shochu too

秋の露 蔵のこだわり.name_en: Aki no Tsuyu Kura no Kodawari

kumamoto:jufuku.tagline_en: Mushagaeshi — atmospheric distillation and clay pots, uncompromised.
kumamoto:jufuku.desc_en: Jufuku Shuzojo, founded in 1890 in Hitoyoshi, distils its famous Mushagaeshi from 100% Kumamoto-grown Hinohikari rice, at atmospheric pressure — the soul of the house — then rests it more than two years, with clay-pot brewing lending its depth.
features_en: Atmospheric distillation as the house soul

kumamoto:takata.tagline_en: Kuma shochu brewed with flower yeasts, since 1902.
kumamoto:takata.desc_en: Takata Shuzojo began shochu making in 1902 under ninth-generation head Matasuke (Kanji Takata). Keeping the Kuma tradition, it also experiments where few do — brewing shochu with flower yeasts, as in its Asagiri no Hana, while the founding label Akiho lives on.

kumamoto:yamato1.tagline_en: Shochu brewed on hot-spring water — and even on milk.
kumamoto:yamato1.desc_en: Yamatoichi Shuzomoto was founded in 1898 by Chimatsu Okada in Hitoyoshi. Its signature is unique in Japan: onsen shochu, brewed with mineral-rich bicarbonate hot-spring water rising from 500 metres beneath the kura. A milk shochu made with fresh local milk pushes the experiments further.
features_en: Hot-spring water from 500m below the kura

kumamoto:fukuda.tagline_en: Quality before efficiency — 37 excellence awards since 1965.
kumamoto:fukuda.desc_en: Fukuda Shuzo was founded in 1935 in Hitoyoshi by Kunihiko Fukuda of Amakusa. Its creed of quality before efficiency shows in the record: 37 excellence awards at the Kumamoto Regional Taxation Bureau appraisal since 1965, won through clean rooms, exact temperatures and patient handling of koji and yeast. Sanga leads the range.

kumamoto:kinoshita.tagline_en: Bunzo — licensed as a teahouse by the Sagara lords in 1862.
kumamoto:kinoshita.desc_en: Kinoshita Jozo, founded in 1862, is among the oldest Kuma shochu houses, licensed as a chaya (teahouse) by the Sagara domain. Its single-minded label Bunzo carries the name of founder Bunzo, sung of in the folk song Rokuchoshi, and the methods are unchanged: hand-made koji, clay-pot fermentation, atmospheric distillation.
features_en: Hand koji, clay pots, atmospheric stills
Bunzo: named in a folk song

kumamoto:matsushita.tagline_en: The oldest kura of Kuma shochu — fourteen generations since 1804.
kumamoto:matsushita.desc_en: Matsushita Jozojo began in 1804, when first-generation Jihei took up shochu making in the Sagara domain's Iwano village — making it the oldest kura of Kuma shochu, now in its fourteenth generation. At the source of the Kuma River in Mizukami, it brews from the valley's people, water and rice, its history bottled plainly in the label Saikogura, the oldest kura.

kumamoto:tsutsumi.tagline_en: Cask, ceramic and bottle — Kuma shochu with a research bent.
kumamoto:tsutsumi.desc_en: Tsutsumi Shuzo was founded in 1878 as the Indo Jozojo and took its present name in 2002. It matures its Kuma shochu across casks, ceramics and bottles, and works with university laboratories on new products — aiming at shochu that can stand anywhere in the world.
features_en: Maturation across cask, ceramic and bottle

kumamoto:miyahara.tagline_en: Stone-chamber koji and cold-season mash on Kuma River water.
kumamoto:miyahara.desc_en: Miyahara Shuzojo of Asagiri brews Kuma shochu the old way: koji rice grown in a traditional stone chamber, cold-season mash on Kuma River subsoil water, atmospheric distillation, then long rest in clay pots — bottled as Kuma Sennin and Miya no Homare.
features_en: Cold-season brewing on Kuma subsoil water

kumamoto:matsumoto.tagline_en: Banryoku — fragrant Kuma shochu from the valley's centre.
kumamoto:matsumoto.desc_en: Matsumoto Shuzojo, founded in 1908 in Asagiri at the near-centre of the Kuma valley, has brewed for over a century, working the basin's rice and clear water into its aromatic, full-flavoured Banryoku.

kumamoto:nasu.tagline_en: Kuma no Izumi — a four-generation family kura of tray koji and clay pots.
kumamoto:nasu.desc_en: Nasu Shuzojo, founded in 1917 in Taragi by Torajiro Nasu, remains a small family kura in its fourth generation. Fine koji from the morobuta tray method, depth from clay-pot fermentation and long storage give its Kuma no Izumi its rich, rounded character.
features_en: Morobuta tray koji and clay-pot brewing

kumamoto:batsugun.tagline_en: Batsugun — a name that promises outstanding, and means to keep it.
kumamoto:batsugun.desc_en: Batsugun Shuzo of Kurohiji in Taragi took its name from its founding wish: to make shochu that is batsugun — outstanding — to drink. The house balances Kuma tradition with new work such as its cask-aged Jukuko Batsugun developed for markets beyond the prefecture.

kumamoto:miyamoto.tagline_en: Three hundred years in Taragi, distilled into Kyudaime.
kumamoto:miyamoto.desc_en: Miyamoto Shuzojo has brewed Kuma shochu in Taragi for more than three hundred years. Its Kyudaime (Ninth Generation), launched in 1994, carries the rice's flavour and sweetness in a rounded, balanced pour.

kumamoto:hayashi.tagline_en: Gokuraku — paradise, aged slow, from a mid-Edo family kura.
kumamoto:hayashi.desc_en: Hayashi Shuzojo, founded in the mid-Edo period in Yunomae, is among the oldest Kuma shochu houses — its fifteenth-generation head keeps the inherited craft with stubborn fidelity, drawing on the well that has flowed since the founding. Its Gokuraku (Paradise) is an atmospheric-distilled rice shochu given long rest.
features_en: The founding well still in use

kumamoto:fuchita.tagline_en: An honoured old kura by the Kuma River, currently at rest.
kumamoto:fuchita.desc_en: Fuchita Shuzojo, re-founded in 1878 on the banks of the Kuma River, took the grand honour prize at Japan's first national liquor fair in 1926 and was chosen to present its shochu to Emperor Showa on his 1931 visit to Kumamoto. Reports indicate the house is currently not in operation.
features_en: Grand honour prize, first national liquor fair (1926)

kumamoto:fuchita_honten.tagline_en: Isshochi — twenty clay pots and all handwork at the valley's last kura downstream.
kumamoto:fuchita_honten.desc_en: Fuchita Shuzo Honten began in 1869 as the Kazaemon Chaya of founder Kazaemon Fuchita, moving to its present site in 1908 when the Hisatsu rail line came through. Everything from koji to washing and mashing is done by hand, with twenty clay pots lining the kura — the furthest downstream of all Kuma shochu houses. Its oak-aged Isshochi borrows the auspicious name of a village whose characters read 'a place of victory'.
features_en: All handwork; twenty clay pots in the kura

kumamoto:zuiyo.tagline_en: Shochu beside sake and red sake, from Kumamoto's all-round house.
kumamoto:zuiyo.desc_en: Zuiyo, founded in 1867 in Kumamoto City and merged with Toyo Jozo in 2001, is the city's all-round brewer: sake, honkaku shochu, ceremonial red sake and liqueurs. Its shochu side includes Tohi Ippon Yari, and the Taisho-era Tohi Taisho Kura opens the old buildings to visitors.
features_en: Sake, shochu, red sake and liqueurs in one house

kumamoto:amakusa.tagline_en: Ike no Tsuyu — the founding imo shochu of Amakusa, revived.
kumamoto:amakusa.desc_en: Amakusa Shuzo, founded in 1899, is the only shochu kura in the Amakusa islands. It began as an imo shochu house, switched to rice and barley in the late Showa period — then fourth-generation head Yutaka Hirashita brought it home, reviving the founding sweet-potato label Ike no Tsuyu.
features_en: The Amakusa islands' only shochu kura
Founding imo shochu revived by the 4th generation

池の露.specs_en: Honkaku imo shochu — the revived founding label

kumamoto:bishounen.tagline_en: The Bishonen sake house's Aso shochus, brewing since 1752.
kumamoto:bishounen.desc_en: Bishonen began brewing in 1752 on the orders of Hosokawa Shigekata, lord of Kumamoto, and restarted in Kikuchi in 2013 after a business transfer. Known nationally for its sake, the house also distils the Kuro Aso and Aka Aso shochus from the blessings of the Aso caldera.

kumamoto:hananooka.tagline_en: The Ubusuna sake house's rice shochu, on Myoken shrine spring water.
kumamoto:hananooka.desc_en: Hananoka Shuzo began in 1902 when Kakuji and Mosaku Kanda took over sacred paddies of the Myoken shrine, brewing as Kanda Shuzo until the 1992 renaming. Nationally celebrated for its sake Hananoka and Ubusuna, the house also distils the rice shochu Wani, on rock-spring water rising at the shrine.
features_en: The nationally watched Hananoka / Ubusuna house

kyoto:takara_shuzo.tagline_en: Takara Shochu and the all-potato Ikkomon, from Fushimi to the world.
kyoto:takara_shuzo.desc_en: Takara Shuzo, founded in 1842 in Fushimi, Kyoto, is one of Japan's great drinks houses. Its Takara Shochu practically defines korui shochu, while Ikkomon — 'the stubborn one' in Satsuma dialect — is a honkaku imo shochu made from 100% sweet potato, koji included. With the sake Sho Chiku Bai it exports to dozens of countries.
features_en: One of Japan's leading shochu makers

mie:miyazaki_honten.tagline_en: Kinmiya — the shochu of Tokyo's old downtown, made in Mie since 1846.
mie:miyazaki_honten.desc_en: Miyazaki Honten, founded in 1846, is famous nationwide for Kinmiya Shochu — the korui shochu that fuels the hoppy and chuhai culture of Tokyo's old downtown. Brewed on Suzuka mountain subsoil water, the house also makes cask-aged barley shochu with consecutive Monde Selection Grand Golds, and holds seventeen straight years of golds at the world liquor competition.

mie:iseman.tagline_en: Ise-Shima's only kura — thirty years of Konen, plus a craft gin.
mie:iseman.desc_en: Iseman, founded in 1949, is the only brewer in Ise-Shima, making shochu, sake and liqueurs. Its Konen barley shochu has run for over thirty years — the Stella Konen version pot-distilled with black koji — and it makes Mie's only craft gin. Tastings at its brewery shop in Okage Yokocho, before the Grand Shrine.
features_en: Mie's only craft gin; shop by the Grand Shrine

miyazaki:kirishima-shuzo.tagline_en: Nine straight years as Japan's best-selling imo shochu.
miyazaki:kirishima-shuzo.desc_en: Kirishima Shuzo, founded in 1916 in Miyakonojo, has held the number-one spot in honkaku imo shochu sales for nine consecutive years. It uses only Kyushu sweet potatoes, Japanese rice and the underground water of the Kirishima range, with capacity around 200,000 1.8-litre bottles a day. Black-koji Kurokirishima (1998) and Akakirishima (2003) lead the range; the Kirishima Factory Garden offers tours, a craft brewery and a bakery.
features_en: Japan's best-selling imo shochu, 9 years running

miyazaki:unkai-shuzo.tagline_en: Inventor of soba shochu (1973), brewing across Miyazaki and Kagoshima.
miyazaki:unkai-shuzo.desc_en: Unkai Shuzo developed Japan's first buckwheat shochu in 1973 and now makes soba, barley and imo shochu across several plants in Miyazaki and Kagoshima — plus sake, wine and craft beer as a full-range drinks maker. The Aya Nature Kura visitor hall and Shusen no Mori estate welcome guests.

miyazaki:kuroki-honten.tagline_en: Hyakunen no Kodoku — farming-first shochu that returns to the soil.
miyazaki:kuroki-honten.desc_en: Kuroki Honten, founded in 1885 in Takanabe, is the house behind Hyakunen no Kodoku (One Hundred Years of Solitude), Nakanaka and Kiroku. Its creed — sake making begins with farming — is lived through its organic farming subsidiary Yomigaeru Daichi no Kai and a circular practice that returns shochu lees to fields as fertiliser and feed. It also runs the Osuzuyama Distillery in the hills.
features_en: Hyakunen no Kodoku and other cult labels
Circular farming: lees back to the fields

miyazaki:yanagita-shuzo.tagline_en: A barley house in imo country, reviving the Miyazaki Hadaka grain.
miyazaki:yanagita-shuzo.desc_en: Yanagita Shuzo, founded in 1902 in Miyakonojo, swims against Miyazaki's sweet-potato current: barley shochu is its main line, under fifth-generation toji Tadashi Yanagita and the motto that ingredients are everything. It works fine Kyushu barley, has revived cultivation of the native Miyazaki Hadaka variety, and distils under vacuum for a clear, clean profile.

miyazaki:akashi-shuzo.tagline_en: Meigetsu — mellow imo-and-rice shochu on Ebino highland water.
miyazaki:akashi-shuzo.desc_en: Akashi Shuzo began when founder Niemon Akashi took up shochu making in Ebino in 1891. Its standard-bearer Meigetsu, launched in 1950, blends sweet potato and rice into a mellow, rounded pour, brewed with fine Ebino highland groundwater and koji from rice the house grows itself.

miyazaki:ochiai-shuzojo.tagline_en: Two-century pots, vegetable shochus, and a bottle named for the hearth cat.
miyazaki:ochiai-shuzojo.desc_en: Ochiai Shuzojo in Miyazaki City, led by fourth-generation toji-president Ryohei Ochiai, runs its first fermentation in clay pots more than two hundred years old and rests everything at least a year and a half. Sweet potatoes come from Miyakonojo contract farmers using green-manure cultivation, and the house even distils vegetable shochus — green pepper, garlic, ginger. It recommends its shochu hot, with food.

miyazaki:watanabe-shuzojo.tagline_en: Eighty percent home-grown — terroir shochu with wild yeasts.
miyazaki:watanabe-shuzojo.desc_en: Watanabe Shuzojo, founded in 1914, is the only kura in the Tano district of Miyazaki. Fourth-generation head Koichiro Watanabe grows Koganesengan on three hectares of the house's own fields — about eighty percent of its ingredients — and brews on the theme of sake from the land that makes it: soil left on the potatoes, wild yeasts and native microbes at work, and about three years of rest before release.

miyazaki:kyoya-shuzo.tagline_en: Organic imo shochu from century-old pots and a Cornish boiler.
miyazaki:kyoya-shuzo.desc_en: Kyoya Shuzo, founded in 1834 in Nichinan, brews with equipment that is itself a museum — clay pots over a century old and a rare Cornish boiler. It holds JAS organic certification through its own farming subsidiary, designs low-alcohol releases for newcomers, and thinks in food pairings.
features_en: JAS organic through its own farm company

miyazaki:oura-shuzo.tagline_en: A monk-turned-distiller's family kura, making rare brown-rice shochu.
miyazaki:oura-shuzo.desc_en: Oura Shuzo of Miyakonojo, founded in 1909, is a small family kura whose fourth-generation head Shinichi Oura came to distilling from life as a Buddhist monk. Koji is made by hand with wooden boxes and futon in the old way, fermentation runs in clay pots, and its brown-rice shochu — developed in 1975 — is made by only a couple of kura in all Japan. A glass wall lets visitors watch the work.
features_en: Hand koji with boxes and futon

miyazaki:sato-shochu.tagline_en: Clay pots by the Hourigawa, with both stills at its command.
miyazaki:sato-shochu.desc_en: Sato Shochu Seizojo, founded in 1905 on the Hourigawa river in Nobeoka, keeps clay-pot brewing while commanding both atmospheric and vacuum distillation. Ingredients come from local farmers through its Kirari-kai circle, and the house extends into peach and chestnut liqueurs. Tours through the glass windows for up to 100, booked a month ahead.

miyazaki:furusawa-jozo.tagline_en: Four grains, one earthen kura, and a woman at the helm.
miyazaki:furusawa-jozo.desc_en: Furusawa Jozo, founded in 1892 in Nichinan, is led by fifth-generation head Masako Furusawa. In its earthen-walled kura the house keeps to natural fermentation and the old ways, distilling all four classic styles — sweet potato, barley, rice and buckwheat — plus the women-focused YAEZAKURA -SEN- brand.
features_en: Led by a woman of the fifth generation

miyazaki:kagura-shuzo.tagline_en: Kurouma barley shochu, cask-aged inside a railway tunnel.
miyazaki:kagura-shuzo.desc_en: Kagura Shuzo, based since 1954 in the myth-country of Takachiho, turned from sake to honkaku shochu and built its name on Kurouma — 100% Japanese barley. Its casks sleep inside a disused railway tunnel at the Tunnel no Eki facility, open for visits and shopping; the imo shochu Tenson Korin honours Takachiho's founding myth.
features_en: Cask ageing in a rail tunnel — Tunnel no Eki

miyazaki:osuzuyama-joryusho.tagline_en: Yamaneko, Yamazaru, Yamasemi — mountain spirits from cedar vats.
miyazaki:osuzuyama-joryusho.desc_en: Osuzuyama Distillery, founded in 1998 as Kuroki Honten's mountain kura, sits thirty minutes into the hills above Takanabe. Ultra-soft mountain spring water, hand-made koji and wooden vessels of local Obi cedar shape its animal-named spirits — Yamaneko (wildcat, sweet potato), Yamazaru (monkey, barley) and Yamasemi (kingfisher, rice) — handwork no machine could copy.
features_en: Ultra-soft spring water and Obi cedar vats

miyazaki:kawagoe-shuzojo.tagline_en: Experience and instinct — a 19th-generation toji, three bottles, no tours.
miyazaki:kawagoe-shuzojo.desc_en: Kawagoe Shuzojo, founded at the end of the Edo period in Kunitomi, brews by the experience and instinct of nineteenth-generation toji Masahiro Kawagoe. Taisho-era clay pots set into the ground still hold the mash, atmospheric distillation keeps the potato and rice character intact, and every bottle is filled, checked and labelled by hand. Just three labels, sold only through trusted merchants; no tours.

miyazaki:sakuranogo-shuzo.tagline_en: Obi cedar vats and gentle vacuum-distilled shochu in Nichinan.
miyazaki:sakuranogo-shuzo.desc_en: Sakuranomine Shuzo, founded in 1877 in Nichinan and led by seventh-generation head Akashi Hashimoto, brews small: clay pots and Obi cedar vats eighty to a hundred years old, with vacuum distillation lending a mellow nose and soft mouthfeel. Seasonal releases and a 40-degree long-aged expression reward the curious.

miyazaki:akugare-joryusho.tagline_en: Shochu is raised, not made — small batches on Mimikawa water.
miyazaki:akugare-joryusho.desc_en: Akugare Distillery in Hyuga, founded in 2004 as Tominotsuyu Shuzo and renamed in 2015, brews in clay pots in small volumes under toji Toyofumi Yamamoto, who holds that shochu is something you raise, not make. Contract-grown Koganesengan and Daichi no Yume potatoes meet the subsoil water of the Mimikawa. Tours by reservation during the August–December brewing season.

miyazaki:ikoma-kogen-shuzo.tagline_en: A 22-degree original from the Ikoma highlands.
miyazaki:ikoma-kogen-shuzo.desc_en: Ikoma Kogen Shuzo was established in 1998 when Akashi Shuzo carried on the licence of Ebihara Shuzo. Its shochu is produced at Akashi's works, led by a signature quirk: a 22-degree strength, deliberately between the standard 20 and 25, in service of local tourism and farming.

miyazaki:suki-shuzo.tagline_en: New wood, old pots — kura-born yeasts in the mountains of Suki.
miyazaki:suki-shuzo.desc_en: Suki Shuzo, founded in 1890 in the mountains near the Kumamoto border, draws fine groundwater from 120 metres down and still ferments in pots more than 160 years old. The toji manages hand-made koji himself — and designs the labels too — while a newly built wooden kura nurtures the house's own resident yeasts. Tours and tastings by reservation.
features_en: New wooden kura raising house yeasts

miyazaki:masaharu-shuzo.tagline_en: Aisome — an idea at 23, perfected over fifteen years.
miyazaki:masaharu-shuzo.desc_en: Masaharu Shuzo of Saito — renamed Yamaya Distillery in 2022 from Meiji-era roots — brews under fifth-generation president Yuto Kuroki to the creed that shochu is local sake, raised from this land's crops, water and air. Local Koganesengan meets the soft (hardness 34) Shimizugane spring; the signature Aisome was conceived when its maker was 23 and took fifteen years to complete. Tours are welcomed.
features_en: Aisome: fifteen years in the making

miyazaki:miyakonojo-shuzo.tagline_en: Good shochu, honest prices — the people's kura of Miyakonojo.
miyazaki:miyakonojo-shuzo.desc_en: Miyakonojo Shuzo, founded in 1956, brews to a plain motto: better shochu, more affordable. Its range spans sweet potato, barley, rice, buckwheat and sesame, and the company extends into hydroponic vegetables and food franchising through its M's Garden farming arm.

miyazaki:inoue-shuzo.tagline_en: Japan's first fully vacuum-distilled imo shochu — and caviar on the side.
miyazaki:inoue-shuzo.desc_en: Inoue Shuzo, founded in 1894 amid the Obi cedar forests of Nichinan, developed Japan's first 100% vacuum-distilled imo shochu in 1983. It brews sweet potato, barley, buckwheat and rice shochu with the Yowara spring — chosen among Miyazaki's 21 famous waters in 1993 — and, remarkably, farms sturgeon for caviar as well.
features_en: Japan's first fully vacuum-distilled imo shochu (1983)
Yowara spring, a Miyazaki famous water

miyazaki:miyata-honten.tagline_en: From vinegar maker to shochu kura — floor koji by a woman toji.
miyazaki:miyata-honten.desc_en: Miyata Honten began in 1804 as a vinegar brewer, turning to shochu in 1921. The house makes koji entirely by hand in the traditional floor method and distils at atmospheric pressure; the koji moulds resident in the old kura give its shochu a taste that belongs to this building alone. Chikako Miyata — the '7.5th' generation — serves as toji.

miyazaki:takachiho-shuzo.tagline_en: All-koji black-koji barley shochu — and a corn shochu — in myth country.
miyazaki:takachiho-shuzo.desc_en: Takachiho Shuzo, founded in 1902 as Tamanotsuyu Shuzo and renamed in 1976, makes barley shochu its main line (60% of production) in a distinctive style: black koji, all-koji mash, atmospheric distillation. Imo shochu and the corn shochu Kariboshi widen the range, and by-products return to livestock feed and aquaculture.
features_en: By-products recycled to feed and aquaculture

miyazaki:matsunotsuyu-shuzo.tagline_en: Mellow imo shochu below Obi castle, on the Sakatani River.
miyazaki:matsunotsuyu-shuzo.desc_en: Matsunotsuyu Shuzo brews on the Sakatani River below the castle town of Obi, chasing shochu that keeps the sweet potato's aroma and umami in an easy, rounded pour. An early adopter of automated koji equipment, it pairs the machines with traditional technique for consistent quality.
features_en: Below the castle town of Obi

miyazaki:akatsuki-shuzo.tagline_en: Nothing has changed — rice shochu held to the old strength.
miyazaki:akatsuki-shuzo.desc_en: Akatsuki Shuzo of Takachiho, founded in 1934 as a sake brewer, now devotes itself to rice shochu alone. Its spirit rests about eighteen months before shipping, offered at 20, 25 and 35 degrees — the 25 most loved — made by methods the house proudly says have never changed. No tours.

miyazaki:himeizumi-shuzo.tagline_en: Unfiltered shochu raised by the yeasts living in a 130-year kura.
miyazaki:himeizumi-shuzo.desc_en: Himeizumi Shuzo, founded in 1831 in Hinokage near Takachiho, is run by its seventh generation. It refuses filtration, keeping the spirit's native umami whole, and credits the resident yeasts of its 130-year-old buildings for a flavour nobody could copy. Barley, sweet potato, buckwheat and glutinous rice all pass through its stills, on spring water from across the river.

miyazaki:iwakura-shuzojo.tagline_en: Same-day potatoes, well water, and every label glued by hand.
miyazaki:iwakura-shuzojo.desc_en: Iwakura Shuzojo in Saito is a small fourth-generation family kura that processes its local sweet potatoes the very day they are dug, brewing with well water alone. Everything from washing and sorting to labelling is done by hand, and the bottles go straight to trusted merchants with no wholesaler between — its signature pours with the gentle sweetness of a steamed sweet potato.
features_en: Direct sales to trusted merchants only

miyazaki:otemon-shuzo.tagline_en: High-temperature fermentation and labels of tatami and rubber.
miyazaki:otemon-shuzo.desc_en: Otemon, founded in 1895 as a family shop in the castle town of Obi, brews by its own high-temperature fermentation method — drawing each ingredient's character out rather than blending it in afterwards. Its five product lines trace the life of Miyamoto Musashi, wrapped by an in-house design team in labels of unexpected materials, tatami and rubber among them.

miyazaki:sakuranosato-shuzo.tagline_en: Five thousand clay pots in a red-brick tower — and a shochu dojo.
miyazaki:sakuranosato-shuzo.desc_en: Sakuranosato Shuzo, founded in 1994 as a subsidiary of Inoue Shuzo, matures its shochu three years and more in some 5,000 clay pots stacked through a three-storey red-brick warehouse, marrying computer control with human judgement. Its Shochu Dojo — a recreation of a Meiji-era kura — offers tours, hands-on experiences and even original blending, on spring water of the Inohae gorge.
features_en: Shochu Dojo visitor hall with blending

miyazaki:shochu-nichinan.tagline_en: Five Nichinan kura and a 12-degree toast for the city's kanpai law.
miyazaki:shochu-nichinan.desc_en: The Shochu Nichinan Cooperative, formed in 1984, unites five local houses — Kyoya, Kodama, Sakuranomine, Furusawa and Matsunotsuyu. Its 12-degree Kanpai Nichinan was created for the city's 2013 toast ordinance: a mellow, low-strength shochu built for Nichinan's table.
features_en: 12-degree shochu for the city's toast ordinance

miyazaki:kozo-shuzo.tagline_en: Pots half-buried in volcanic ash, every step by hand.
miyazaki:kozo-shuzo.desc_en: Kozo Shuzo of Kushima, founded in 1919 and renamed in 2003, works entirely by hand — mash, fermentation, distillation and bottling — in unglazed clay pots sunk halfway into the volcanic-ash earth. Yeasts living in the kura's old wooden walls round the spirit, brewed from on-site spring water and local ingredients. No tours.
features_en: Pots half-buried in volcanic ash soil

miyazaki:shoro-shuzo.tagline_en: Farmers' shochu — rich and strong, from a kura its growers own.
miyazaki:shoro-shuzo.desc_en: Shoro Shuzo began in 1928 as the Ubagasako shochu venture of about ten local farming families, taking its present name in 1971. Under third-generation head Shoji Yano it refuses the light modern style, distilling full-bodied, robust imo shochu on volcanic-ash-filtered groundwater with the kura's own yeasts. Its toji still farms — entering the kura only for the September–December brewing season.
features_en: A toji who farms the rest of the year

miyazaki:kodama-jozo.tagline_en: An 1818 Obi kura reborn in 2001, brewed by a farm-school toji.
miyazaki:kodama-jozo.desc_en: Kodama Jozo, founded in 1818 in the castle town of Obi and revived in 2001, brews in small volumes under toji Junpei Kanamaru, trained at Tokyo University of Agriculture, who moves between hand-made koji and machine as each batch demands. Miyazaki Beni and Koganemasari potatoes go into bottles the house calls one soul at a time. No tours.

miyazaki:jukai-shuzo.tagline_en: Five century-old kura in one, feeding its lees back to the land.
miyazaki:jukai-shuzo.desc_en: Jukai Shuzo was formed in 1985 when five distilleries — each with over a century of history — merged into a cooperative in Kushima. Miyazaki Beni red sweet potatoes and spring water rising on the grounds give a soft, sweetly fragrant pour, and the lees feed livestock in a working circular farm system.
features_en: Miyazaki Beni potatoes and on-site spring

nagasaki:ikinohana.tagline_en: Iki no Hana — atmospheric stills on the island where barley shochu began.
nagasaki:ikinohana.desc_en: Iki no Hana was founded in 1900 when Kasuke Nagata crossed from Kokura to Iki — the island recognised by GI Iki as the birthplace of barley shochu, five centuries deep in the craft. The house holds to atmospheric distillation and patient maturation for its fragrant island shochu. Tours 9:00–17:00, groups by reservation.

nagasaki:ikinokura.tagline_en: Six island houses, one kura — tradition with flower yeasts and FSSC certification.
nagasaki:ikinokura.desc_en: Iki no Kura Shuzo was formed in 1984 by the full cooperation of six Iki brewing companies. Keeping the island's 16th-century technique, it experiments freely — vacuum distillation, flower-yeast brewing — and holds FSSC 22000 food-safety certification (2019) under GI Iki. Tours by reservation.
features_en: Six companies merged, GI Iki certified

nagasaki:genkai.tagline_en: Iki — the standard-bearer of the island's 500-year barley shochu.
nagasaki:genkai.desc_en: Genkai Shuzo, founded in 1900, is the flag-carrier of GI Iki barley shochu, heir to the island's five-hundred-year tradition. Its Mugi Shochu Iki won Monde Selection honours eleven years running from 2002, crowned by the Crystal Prestige Trophy in 2011; the Super Gold editions rest in white-oak casks.

nagasaki:omoya.tagline_en: Ninety percent island-grown, clay-pot brewed — and a sake revival by two brothers.
nagasaki:omoya.desc_en: Omoya Shuzo, founded in 1924 by Kakuzo Yokoyama, brews GI Iki shochu from more than 90% Iki-grown ingredients in traditional clay pots, switching between white and black koji. Brothers run the house — Yuzo as shochu toji, Taizo as sake toji — and in 2018 they revived sake brewing on the island after some thirty years with their Yokoyama label.
features_en: Sake brewing revived in 2018 by the brothers

nagasaki:amanogawa.tagline_en: Amanogawa — the Milky Way, aged long over atmospheric stills.
nagasaki:amanogawa.desc_en: Amanogawa Shuzo, founded in 1912 under GI Iki, holds to atmospheric distillation for barley shochu rich in grain aroma, then lets time do its work: twelve- and fifteen-year maturations, ten years in clay pots for one bottling, and an oak-aged Monkey Rock for the adventurous.

nagasaki:sarukawa_izu.tagline_en: Sacred spring water and ultrasonic ageing on the Sarukawa riverbank.
nagasaki:sarukawa_izu.desc_en: Sarukawa Izu Shuzo, founded in 1903 on the banks of the Sarukawa, brews GI Iki shochu with spring water so clear it has long been called the water of the gods. Two-thirds barley to one-third rice koji, atmospheric distillation, the founding recipe unchanged — plus one modern twist: the industry's first ultrasonic maturation.

nagasaki:yamanomori.tagline_en: Iki's oldest kura — clay pots for both mashes, each one unique.
nagasaki:yamanomori.desc_en: Yamanomori Shuzojo, founded in 1899, is the oldest kura on Iki, and the only one on the island to run both first and second mash in clay pots — hand-made vessels from the founding era, each of a slightly different size. Gold at the Fukuoka bureau appraisal (2012) crowns its GI Iki craft.
features_en: Clay pots for both mashes — unique on the island

nagasaki:fukuda.tagline_en: Jagatara Oharu — shochu with a trading-port story, at Japan's western edge.
nagasaki:fukuda.desc_en: Fukuda Shuzo, founded in 1688 in Hirado and purveyor to the Hirado domain, is the westernmost brewery on Japan's main islands. Beside its sake Fukutsuru it distils shochu with names straight from Hirado's trading-port history — Jagatara Oharu, for the exiled girl of the Jakarta letters, and Kapitan, for the Dutch traders' chief.

nagasaki:mori.tagline_en: Hiran — Hirado terroir from the old Komatsuya trading house.
nagasaki:mori.desc_en: Mori Shuzojo was founded in 1895 by Kokichi Mori under the shop name Komatsuya, in Hirado's old international port. The fourth-generation head brews to a theme of continuity and connection, expressing Hirado's terroir with spring water of Saikyoji temple and local rice — in the sake Hiran, named for Hirado's ancient name, and its shochu.
features_en: Founded 1895 in the old port of Hirado
Saikyoji spring water and local rice

nagasaki:umegae.tagline_en: Shochu, sake and gin inside seven cultural-property buildings.
nagasaki:umegae.desc_en: Umegae Shuzo, founded in 1787 in Sasebo, still works inside its Edo-period buildings — seven of them registered National Tangible Cultural Properties. The house makes sake, shochu, liqueurs and a Japanese gin; its Ginta shochu is a two-time consecutive gold winner. Tours by reservation, with kura-opening festivals twice a year.

nagasaki:imazato.tagline_en: 250 years in Hasami, brewing Rokujuyoshu for all of Japan.
nagasaki:imazato.desc_en: Imazato Shuzo, founded in 1772 in the porcelain town of Hasami, has brewed for a quarter-millennium in buildings that remember it — six are registered cultural properties, the main and middle kura dating near the founding. Its label Rokujuyoshu means the sixty-odd provinces: a sake, and shochu, meant for the whole country.
features_en: Rokujuyoshu: named for all Japan's provinces

六十餘洲.specs_en: The house label — named for Japan's sixty-odd provinces

nagasaki:kinokawa.tagline_en: Isahaya's only kura, pouring at its Yokayoka factory shop.
nagasaki:kinokawa.desc_en: Kinokawa, founded in 1839, is the only brewery in Isahaya — more than 180 years under its creed of raising good people and good sake, brewing with local ingredients and Kumamoto yeast. In 2023 it opened the Yokayoka factory shop at the kura.

nagasaki:oshima.tagline_en: A town-built kura growing its own red sweet potatoes by the sea.
nagasaki:oshima.desc_en: Oshima Shuzo was founded in 1985 as a third-sector venture of Saikai city, the farm and fishery cooperatives and private partners, to bring life to the island town. It grows its own red sweet potatoes from planting to harvest, brews by hand — and in 2018 raised a new kura with modern equipment. Brandy-cask-aged barley shochu and first-run bottlings colour the range.
features_en: Grows its own red sweet potatoes

磨き大島.specs_en: Ginjo-style imo shochu, red sweet potatoes

nagasaki:kubo.tagline_en: The phantom barley shochu — micro-vacuum stills and four years' patience.
nagasaki:kubo.desc_en: Kubo Shuzojo, founded in 1907, is a small family kura using only Isahaya-grown barley. Its invention is a distillation between atmospheric and vacuum — micro-vacuum — and its discipline is time: four years and more in stainless tanks before release. The soft, mellow result has earned its label the nickname of the phantom barley shochu.

nagasaki:gotonadashuzou.tagline_en: Nagasaki's only imo shochu kura — farming and distilling as one.
nagasaki:gotonadashuzou.desc_en: Gotonada Shuzo, founded in 2007 in Shin-Kamigoto, is the only imo shochu kura in Nagasaki Prefecture. Its banner is noujo-goitsu — farming and brewing as one: 100% of its sweet potatoes are grown on Kamigoto, on its own farm and by contract growers, in a circular system that even revives heirloom varieties like the native Kinboke.

nagasaki:gotoretto.tagline_en: Everything island-grown — barley and imo shochu of Fukue.
nagasaki:gotoretto.desc_en: Goto Retto Shuzo, established in 2008, is Fukue Island's only honkaku shochu maker, shipping since July 2009. Its creed is simple: every ingredient island-raised. Goto barley, Goto sweet potatoes and spring water of the Nanatake range fill its Goto Mugi — aged over two years — and Goto Imo. Tours by reservation.

nagasaki:muhyo.tagline_en: Three iTi stars, three years running, from a hillside above the sea.
nagasaki:muhyo.desc_en: Muhyo Shuzo, established around 1990 on the Sotome hills of Nagasaki, brews clay-pot imo and barley shochu. Its barley shochu — from Isahaya-grown Nishinohoshi — took three stars at the International Taste Institute three years running, a Crystal award in 2019 and the Diamond taste award in 2024, with red- and purple-potato companions in its series.
features_en: Clay-pot brewing above the Sotome coast
iTi three stars, three years running

nagasaki:yamasaki.tagline_en: A hundred drinks from the Unzen springs, distilling since 1702.
nagasaki:yamasaki.desc_en: Yamasaki Honten Shuzojo, founded in 1688 in Shimabara, has devoted itself to brewing since 1884 and first distilled shochu as early as 1702. On the famous spring waters of Unzen it now makes more than a hundred products — sake, shochu and liqueurs — with an IWC 2012 award among its honours.

nagasaki:aimusume.tagline_en: Hand-made sake and shochu at the water place below Unzen.
nagasaki:aimusume.desc_en: Aimusume Shuzo, founded in 1873 in Aino — the town on the western Shimabara Peninsula long called the place of water — has brewed by hand for over 150 years at the foot of Unzen, making both sake and shochu on the mountain's clear springs.

nagasaki:kawachi.tagline_en: Tsushima Yamaneko — the island's only kura, named for its wildcat.
nagasaki:kawachi.desc_en: Kawachi Shuzo, founded in 1919 and renamed Shiratake Shuzo in October 2023, is the only brewery on Tsushima, making sake, shochu and liqueurs for about a century. Its Tsushima Yamaneko blends barley and rice shochu 80:20 — a rare recipe whose name winks at the island's wildcat and at old slang for moonshine — while the sake Shiratake holds three straight national golds.
features_en: Sake Shiratake: three straight national golds

nagasaki:yoshidaya.tagline_en: Ninety koku a year, pressed on a hanging beam — with a café at the kura.
nagasaki:yoshidaya.desc_en: Yoshidaya, founded in 1912 in Minamishimabara, brews about ninety koku a year — tiny even by craft standards — and presses its sake by the hanegi method, a hanging wooden beam almost vanished from Japan. Flower yeasts from Tokyo University of Agriculture colour the brewing, and cafe kULa (opened 2023) serves visitors, closed Tuesdays.

nara:nara_kasugayama.tagline_en: A leek shochu, a sweet-potato dream — Nara's playful distiller.
nara:nara_kasugayama.desc_en: Nara Kasugayama Shuzo, founded in 1877 and renamed from Yagi Shuzo in 2022, makes sake, shochu, mirin, liqueurs and spirits at the foot of the Kasuga hills. Its shochu bench is unusually playful: a Yamato barley shochu, a sweet-potato shochu — and even a green-onion shochu. Direct sales at the kura.
features_en: Barley, sweet potato — even leek shochu

niigata:hakkaisan.tagline_en: Rice shochu brewed like Hakkaisan sake — three stages, yellow koji.
niigata:hakkaisan.desc_en: Hakkaisan Brewery turns its sake technique directly into shochu: its rice shochu Yoroshiku Senman Arubeshi is built on a three-stage sake mash with sake yeast and yellow koji, vacuum-distilled and rested over two years. Tours at the company's Uonuma no Sato complex.
features_en: 2+ years maturation; Uonuma no Sato visits

よろしく千萬あるべし.specs_en: Rice shochu on a sake-style mash

oita:sanwa-shurui.tagline_en: iichiko — the barley shochu that carried Oita to every izakaya in Japan.
oita:sanwa-shurui.desc_en: Sanwa Shurui, founded in 1958 in Usa, is one of Japan's largest shochu makers and the house of iichiko, the barley shochu whose 1979 debut became a national phenomenon and made Oita mugi shochu a byword.
