Under its Quality First creed it selects barley and water exactingly, and runs the Hita Distillery and the Ajimu winery as a full-range drinks company.
features_en: One of Japan's largest shochu makers
Hita Distillery and Ajimu winery in the group

oita:nikaido-shuzo.tagline_en: The inventor of all-barley shochu — eight generations in Hiji.
oita:nikaido-shuzo.desc_en: Nikaido Shuzo, founded in 1866 and now in its eighth generation, changed shochu history: it established barley-koji production in 1951, perfected an all-barley shochu in 1973 and launched it in 1974 — igniting the Oita mugi shochu boom. A 1979 agriculture ministry award crowned the achievement, and the Nikaido Art Museum stands beside the kura, brewing under the words of a heart that remembers home.
features_en: Nikaido Art Museum at the kura

oita:yotsuya-shuzo.tagline_en: Kanehachi — roasted-barley depth so loved it's hard to find.
oita:yotsuya-shuzo.desc_en: Yotsuya Shuzo, founded in 1919 in Usa, names its famous shochu for founder Kanehachi Yotsuya. Atmospheric distillation draws out the barley's toasty aroma and dense umami — a flavour fans compare to chocolate-coated barley puffs — and demand has long outrun supply.

oita:fujii-jozo.tagline_en: Weight over ease — all-atmospheric, all-handwork since 1929.
oita:fujii-jozo.desc_en: Fujii Jozo of Bungo-Ono has made barley shochu entirely by hand since 1929. Its Tokujo Taimei, named for the second-generation toji, is 100% atmospheric-distilled — toasty, heavy, satisfying — a house that chooses drinkability last and character first.

oita:jotokuya-shuzojo.tagline_en: Local naked barley, two stills, and citrus liqueurs from Usa.
oita:jotokuya-shuzojo.desc_en: Jotokuya Shuzojo began as a sake kura in 1907, turned to shochu in 1984, and since 2003 has built its Jotokuya brand on fine local naked barley — offered clean from the vacuum still and fragrant from the atmospheric one. Kabosu liqueur and yuzu wine round out the house.
features_en: Kabosu and yuzu on the side

oita:oimatsu-shuzo.tagline_en: Enma — long-aged barley shochu named for the king of hell.
oita:oimatsu-shuzo.desc_en: Oimatsu Shuzo, founded in 1789 in the shogunal water town of Hita and now in its eleventh generation, began as a sake kura and took up shochu in 1970. Its Enma — named for the underworld's judge — is a long-aged barley shochu built on Hita's famous waters.

oita:yatsushika-shuzo.tagline_en: Ginza no Suzume — sparrows of the night, distilled since 1864.
oita:yatsushika-shuzo.desc_en: Yatsushika Shuzo, founded in 1864 in Kokonoe and seven generations on, brews sake, shochu and liqueurs. Its matured shochu Ginza no Suzume — the sparrows of Ginza — toasts the barflies who once talked away the Tokyo night, while the sake Yatsushika carries the house name.
features_en: Sake and shochu in one house

oita:nakano-shuzo.tagline_en: Chiebijin's kura, drawing rice shochu from 200 metres down.
oita:nakano-shuzo.desc_en: Nakano Shuzo, founded in 1874 in the castle town of Kitsuki, brews with mineral-rich water from 200 metres underground and local ingredients — local production for local tables. Its Chiebijin, named for the first landlady Chie, is acclaimed at home and abroad. Tours by reservation, 9:00–16:00.
features_en: Chiebijin: honoured at home and abroad

oita:kuge-honten.tagline_en: A lord's gift kura gone all-local, in UNESCO food town Usuki.
oita:kuge-honten.desc_en: Kuge Honten was founded in 1860 when the lord Inaba Akimichi granted the family a brewing house. Aiming at sake and shochu with character that fits the local table, it switched all ingredients to Oita-grown — especially Usuki-grown — from 2021, a circular kura in a UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy. Tours by reservation for up to thirty.

oita:agataya-shuzo.tagline_en: Quality over quantity since 1712, in the Ajimu basin.
oita:agataya-shuzo.desc_en: Agataya Shuzo, founded in 1712, is among the oldest houses in Oita. In the Ajimu basin — big temperature swings, clear spring water off Mt. Yufu — it carries sake technique into shochu with a plain rule: quality before volume. Tours by reservation, up to ten.

oita:asahi-shuzo.tagline_en: Yaba Bijin — pure-rice shochu once judged the best in Japan.
oita:asahi-shuzo.desc_en: Asahi Shuzo of Nakatsu, founded in 1935, is a rarity in Oita: a junmai (pure rice) shochu house. Its Yaba Bijin — named for the legend that the Yabakei gorge raises beauties — won the top honour at the 6th National Tax Agency appraisal in 1982, built on cool fermentation, gentle distillation and long rest.
features_en: Judged Japan's best at the 1982 appraisal
Cool ferment, gentle still, long rest

oita:inoue-shuzo.tagline_en: Momosuke — shochu of the shogunal water town of Hita.
oita:inoue-shuzo.desc_en: Inoue Shuzo, founded in 1804 in Hita — the old shogunal enclave famous for its waters — brews the sake Kado no I and the honkaku shochu Momosuke on the basin's famed springs.

oita:kuncho-shuzo.tagline_en: Five old kura in Mameda-machi, one dating to 1702.
oita:kuncho-shuzo.desc_en: Kuncho Shuzo, founded in 1932, brews inside the preserved merchant quarter of Mameda-machi in Hita — a nationally designated historic district. Its five kura buildings survive as they were, the oldest raised in 1702; sake, shochu and amazake flow from them, with the Kuncho Shukan shop open daily 9:00–16:30.

oita:aso-honten.tagline_en: Bungo Fuji — hand-made sake and shochu under Mt. Yufu.
oita:aso-honten.desc_en: Aso Honten, founded in 1868 in the green spring-water country of Shonai in Yufu, makes sake and shochu by traditional handwork. Its Bungo Fuji takes the affectionate name of Mt. Yufu — Oita's own Fuji — with the shochu Aso Fujiko a local favourite.

oita:kayashima-shurui.tagline_en: A merchant-house kura on the famous waters of Taketa.
oita:kayashima-shurui.desc_en: Kayashima Shurui began operating in 2009 in Taketa, its merchant-style building set to the castle town's distinctive streetscape. On Taketa's famous spring water it distils a barley shochu of smooth mouthfeel and toasty umami in fine balance.

oita:fujii-shuzo.tagline_en: The Manrikiya house — gold-medal sake and Bungo barley shochu.
oita:fujii-shuzo.desc_en: Fujii Shuzo, founded in 1872 under the shop name Manrikiya in Notsu, Usuki, brews both sake and honkaku shochu. Its sake Ryubai takes gold at the appraisals almost yearly, while the shochus Manrikiya and Bungo carry the house name into the glass.

oita:kotegawa-shuzo.tagline_en: Sorin sake and Hakuju shochu in a novelist's birthplace.
oita:kotegawa-shuzo.desc_en: Kotegawa Shuzo has brewed by hand since 1855 in Usuki. Its 150-year white-walled storehouse is a registered cultural property, and the kura is the birthplace of novelist Yaeko Nogami. The sake Sorin — for the Christian daimyo — and the Oita barley shochu Hakuju lead the range. Tours by reservation.

oita:kuramitsu-shuzo.tagline_en: Oita City's only kura, medalled from the IWC to the US.
oita:kuramitsu-shuzo.desc_en: Kuramitsu Shuzo, founded in 1864, is the only brewery in Oita City, brewing mainly from prefecture-grown Hinohikari rice. Its Soju holds gold at the US National Sake Appraisal, IWC silver and first place at the national liquor concours.
features_en: Golds and medals across three competitions

oita:akamine-shuzojo.tagline_en: The kura of Kichiyomu-san, teller of Oita's tall tales.
oita:akamine-shuzojo.desc_en: Akamine Shuzojo, founded in 1868 in Notsu, Usuki, inherited its buildings from Kichiemon Hirota — the real man behind Kichiyomu-san, hero of Oita's beloved trickster tales. More than 150 years on, the house distils the honkaku shochu Dotton.
features_en: The birthplace of folk hero Kichiyomu-san

oita:yamada-shuzojo.tagline_en: Toyonoseki — aged stock from Bungotakada's only kura.
oita:yamada-shuzojo.desc_en: Yamada Shuzojo, founded in 1898, is the only brewery in Bungotakada. Its Toyonoseki was named with a dream — to become the ozeki, the champion, of Bungo province — and today the house bottles mainly pasteurised, cellar-aged koshu.

oita:ono-shuzo-shonai.tagline_en: A family kura of Yufu, distilling by the founding method.
oita:ono-shuzo-shonai.desc_en: Ono Shuzo, founded in 1906 in the Shonai district of Yufu, is a small family house keeping its founding methods, distilling individual barley shochus from local ingredients under the labels Yufu no Sato and Yufudake.

oita:yano-shuzojo.tagline_en: Matsu no Tsuyu — no added sugar, just Hinohikari sweetness.
oita:yano-shuzojo.desc_en: Yano Shuzojo, founded in 1883 in Kunisaki, took its shop name Matsushimaya — and its label Matsu no Tsuyu — from the pine-and-island view that captivated its founder. A small hand-making house, it brews from Oita Hinohikari rice with no added sugar at all, letting the grain's own sweetness lead.

oita:minami-shuzo.tagline_en: Toppai — two sisters, small batches, and a candy shop at the kura.
oita:minami-shuzo.desc_en: Minami Shuzo, founded in 1868 in Kunisaki, began as a sake kura, restarted with rice shochu after the war, and found its fame in the fifth generation with the barley shochu Toppai — mellow, clean and well loved. Today two sisters keep the family house, refusing mass production; an old-fashioned candy shop shares the grounds.
features_en: A dagashi candy shop on site

oita:mincho-shuho.tagline_en: Purveyor to Usa Jingu, named from an eighth-century chronicle.
oita:mincho-shuho.desc_en: Mincho Shuho was founded in the Kansei era (1790s) as a branch of the Tsushimaya house, and serves as purveyor to the great shrine of Usa Jingu. Its name comes from the Shoku Nihongi: the priest Horen healed the people with sake, and they gathered like the tide — min-cho, the people's tide. In wartime it supplied the Usa naval air corps.
features_en: Named from the Shoku Nihongi chronicle

oita:daichi-shuzo.tagline_en: Hanaemi — rice and koji only, a Saiki tradition carried on.
oita:daichi-shuzo.desc_en: Daichi Shuzo, founded in 1885 in Saiki, was carried forward in 2019 through a business succession that moved the kura to Kamiura — preserving Saiki's sake and shochu culture. Its Hanaemi, brewed from rice and koji alone, is named for the wish of a smile blooming like a flower.

oita:murezuru-shuzo.tagline_en: Mountain-spring barley shochu in the valleys below Mt. Sobo.
oita:murezuru-shuzo.desc_en: Murezuru Shuzo began in 1904 when founder Tamaki Mori brewed the sake Murezuru; the house turned to shochu in the 1980s. In the valley folds of Asaji in Bungo-Ono — ringed by Sobo, Kuju and Aso — it distils small-batch barley shochu on the mountains' spring water.
features_en: Valley kura ringed by Kyushu's great peaks

oita:hamashima-shuzo.tagline_en: Takakiya — grow it yourself, brew it yourself, press it in the fune.
oita:hamashima-shuzo.desc_en: Hamashima Shuzo, founded in 1889 in Bungo-Ono, took its shop name Takakiya from the hawk that landed on the roof beam at the raising. Since 1997 the fifth-generation owner has brewed as toji under a creed of jiko-jijo — grow it yourself, brew it yourself — farming thirteen hectares of sake rice and pressing everything in a traditional fune. The Sasara tearoom serves visitors 9:00–17:00.

oita:sato-shuzo.tagline_en: Kuju Senbazuru — a name given over tea with Kawabata Yasunari.
oita:sato-shuzo.desc_en: Sato Shuzo, founded in 1917, is the only sake kura in the Kuju highlands of Taketa. Its Kuju Senbazuru was named after the novelist Yasunari Kawabata visited Kuju in 1952 while writing the sequel to Thousand Cranes and befriended the brewery's president. The house also pioneered kimoto brewing in Oita.

okayama:miyashita_shuzo.tagline_en: Mint, lotus root, millet — Okayama's laboratory of unusual shochu.
okayama:miyashita_shuzo.desc_en: Miyashita Shuzo, the Okayama all-rounder founded in 1915, distils an unusually wide shochu bench beside its sake and Doppo beer: rice, barley, sweet potato and buckwheat — plus true rarities like mint, lotus-root and millet shochu, with a German hybrid still installed in 2015. The Doppokan brewery complex offers tours, a restaurant and a shop.
features_en: Rare mint, lotus-root and millet shochus

okinawa:iheya_shuzo.tagline_en: Terushima — awamori of the Amaterasu legend, from Iheya's only distillery.
okinawa:iheya_shuzo.desc_en: Iheya Shuzosho was founded in 1948 as a cooperative of 23 islanders and remains the only distillery on Iheya Island. Its flagship Terushima takes its name from the island's legend of the sun goddess Amaterasu, distilled full and rich — rice-sweet with a gentle roast — on mountain spring water and the island air.
features_en: Named from the island's Amaterasu legend

okinawa:izena_shuzo.tagline_en: Tokiwa — crane-and-turtle awamori from the Isle of Evergreen.
okinawa:izena_shuzo.desc_en: Izena Shuzosho, founded in 1949, is the only distillery on Izena Island. Its Tokiwa borrows the island's old epithet — the evergreen isle — with the lucky crane and turtle on its label, offered from standard 30-degree to a 44-degree coarse-filtered bottling made for laying down as kusu.

okinawa:yanbaru_shuzo.tagline_en: Maruta — seven-tenths drunk at home, at the wild north's open door.
okinawa:yanbaru_shuzo.desc_en: Yanbaru Shuzo began in 1950 as the Takazato Shuzosho, funded by the villagers of Ogimi's Takazato district, taking its present name in 2017. About seventy percent of its Maruta is drunk right there in the community — and the distillery is the northernmost on Okinawa's main island that welcomes visitors.

okinawa:nakijin_shuzo.tagline_en: The first 20-degree awamori, beside the walls of Nakijin castle.
okinawa:nakijin_shuzo.desc_en: Nakijin Shuzo, founded in 1948 as Oshiro Shuzo and renamed in 1972, is the only distillery in Nakijin village, near the World Heritage castle ruin. In 1981 it launched the industry's first 20-degree awamori under its Utsukushiki Furusato label — a hit that opened the drink to new drinkers — and it still balances tradition against experiment. Tours are offered.

okinawa:yamakawa_shuzo.tagline_en: The kusu house of Motobu — twenty-year-old awamori in the glass.
okinawa:yamakawa_shuzo.desc_en: Yamakawa Shuzo, founded in 1946, is Motobu's only awamori distillery and is known simply as the kusu Yamakawa — a house given to aged awamori, brewed on spring water from the Yanbaru hills. Visitors can even taste a twenty-year kusu at the distillery.

okinawa:ryusen_shuzo.tagline_en: Old koji and enamel-tank rest below Mt. Tano, since 1939.
okinawa:ryusen_shuzo.desc_en: Ryusen Shuzo, founded in 1939 in the Haneji district of Nago, brews at the foot of Mt. Tano with clear water and hine-koji — aged koji — in every label. Its spirit rests in enamel tanks, emerging soft and mature in aroma. Tours on enquiry.

okinawa:tsukayama_shuzo.tagline_en: The last pre-war distillery standing — a red-tiled Important Cultural Property.
okinawa:tsukayama_shuzo.desc_en: Tsukayama Shuzosho, founded around 1924 in the famous-waters town of Nago, works inside red-tiled wooden buildings raised between 1927 and 1929 — the only distillery in Okinawa preserving its pre-war form, designated a National Important Cultural Property in 2009. Its Kokka pours at a serious 43 degrees. The buildings may be visited.
features_en: In the famous-waters town of Nago

okinawa:helios_shuzo.tagline_en: Six licences, one copper still — Okinawa's spirits all-rounder.
okinawa:helios_shuzo.desc_en: Helios Shuzo, founded in 1961 in Nago, holds six production licences — awamori, spirits, whisky, liqueur, beer and happoshu — and runs Okinawa's only copper pot still. In its ivy-clad kusu warehouse deep in the Yanbaru green, aged awamori sleeps beside craft beer and whisky. Tours with tastings; shop on site.

okinawa:onna_shuzo.tagline_en: Manza — awamori of the scenic cape, mostly drunk within sight of it.
okinawa:onna_shuzo.desc_en: Onna Shuzosho was founded in 1949 by ten village investors and remains Onna's only distillery. Its Manza is named for the Manzamo cape nearby and the wish to be loved by all — fitting, since more than half its production is drunk in the village itself. The house also supports local coral reef conservation.
features_en: Over half its awamori drunk locally

okinawa:sakimoto_shuzo.tagline_en: The kura of the father of awamori's revival, since 1902.
okinawa:sakimoto_shuzo.desc_en: Sakimoto Shuzo, founded in 1902 in Shuri, carries one of awamori's proudest stories: second-generation Seiryo Sakumoto laboured to restore awamori brewing from the ashes of the war, earning the name father of awamori's revival. The house brews with aged koji and deliberately light filtration, keeping aroma and umami in the glass. Tours through the glass gallery on enquiry.
features_en: The father of awamori's post-war revival

okinawa:sakiyama_shuzo.tagline_en: Matsufuji — three-day koji on sacred mountain water.
okinawa:sakiyama_shuzo.desc_en: Sakiyama Shuzosho, founded in 1905 in Kin, brews with natural mountain spring water and a three-day koji that deepens its umami. Its Matsufuji line took first place in the kusu division of the national liquor concours in 2014 and the tax agency commissioner's award in 2025, with moromi vinegar beside the awamori. Tours by reservation.

okinawa:kin_shuzo.tagline_en: Thirteen thousand kusu jars sleeping in a limestone cave.
okinawa:kin_shuzo.desc_en: Kin Shuzo, founded in 1949, named its Tatsu for the founder's dragon-year ancestor and stores more than half its production for ageing. Since 1988 it has used the Kin limestone cave as Japan's first cave kusu cellar — over 13,000 jars sleep in its constant cool — while the brewing splits hard water for the mash and soft for dilution. It even made Japan's first taro shochu. The cave cellar can be visited.

okinawa:kamimura_shuzo.tagline_en: Danryu — the first oak-aged awamori, resting in an underground cellar.
okinawa:kamimura_shuzo.desc_en: Kamimura Shuzo, founded in 1882 in Naha and settled since 1999 below the Ishikawa highlands of Uruma, changed awamori's course in 1968 with Danryu — the industry's first oak-cask-aged awamori. Its underground cellar holds temperature and humidity steady for kusu making, and its five-senses distillery tour (reserved, 1–15 people) ends in tastings.

okinawa:chuko_shuzo.tagline_en: The world's only distillery with its own pottery kiln for kusu jars.
okinawa:chuko_shuzo.desc_en: Chuko Shuzo, founded in 1949 as Oshiro Shuzosho in Tomigusuku, is unique in the world: a distillery that fires its own clay jars at its Ryukyu Gusuku-yaki kiln. Some 600 kusu jars rest in its wooden warehouse, hand-made awamori flows from the Moon Distillery experience hall, and THE OWNERS programme will keep your kusu maturing for up to twenty years. Ten minutes from Naha Airport; tours welcome.
features_en: ~600 kusu jars in a wooden cellar
Moon Distillery hands-on hall; 20-year kusu custody

okinawa:higa_shuzo.tagline_en: Zanpa — the teacher's awamori that became Okinawa's favourite.
okinawa:higa_shuzo.desc_en: Higa Shuzo was founded in 1948 in Yomitan by Torakichi Higa, a schoolteacher who wanted to give Okinawans good awamori. His Zanpa series now ranks among the island's best-loved — the black-label Zanpa Kuro is affectionately called Zankuro across generations, and the premium five-year kusu holds ITI two-star honours. Kusu cellar tours by reservation.

okinawa:shinzato_shuzo.tagline_en: Okinawa's oldest distillery (1846) — from Shuri's thirty licensed masters.
okinawa:shinzato_shuzo.desc_en: Shinzato Shuzo, founded in 1846 in Shuri's Akata quarter, is the oldest surviving distillery in Okinawa, descended from the thirty artisans licensed to brew awamori in the royal quarter of Shuri Sanka. Seven generations on, it pairs that lineage with world-standard quality control — and even a single malt whisky, Ryuka. Tours by reservation, with tastings.
features_en: Descended from Shuri's thirty licensed brewers
Single malt Ryuka beside the awamori

okinawa:chatan_chouro_shuzo.tagline_en: Chatan Choro — a royal-era house carried from Shuri to the coast.
okinawa:chatan_chouro_shuzo.desc_en: Chatan Choro Shuzo began in 1848 as Tamanaha Shuzo in the royal quarter of Shuri, moved to Chatan in 1910, restarted after the war and incorporated under its present name in 2006 — more than 170 years of awamori, and the only distillery in Chatan. Long-aged kusu at 25 and 43 degrees flank the standard.

okinawa:ishikawa_shuzo.tagline_en: Gyokuyu — the best of friends, brewed wholly in clay jars.
okinawa:ishikawa_shuzo.desc_en: Ishikawa Shuzojo, founded in 1949 in Shuri and settled in Nishihara since 1990, is the only house in Okinawa still fermenting its entire production in traditional one-koku clay jars. Its Gyokuyu means the finest of friends, and the craft runs with ISO 9001 discipline (certified 2003). Tours in business hours.

okinawa:shikina_shuzo.tagline_en: Shigure — the first bottled awamori of the post-war, with 150-year kusu in the cellar.
okinawa:shikina_shuzo.desc_en: Shikina Shuzo, founded in 1918 in one of Shuri Sanka's royal brewing quarters, made history twice: its Shigure was the first awamori bottled and labelled for sale in post-war Okinawa, and its cellar holds what is said to be the oldest disclosed kusu in the prefecture — about 150 years old.
features_en: Of the royal Shuri Sanka quarters

okinawa:mizuho_shuzo.tagline_en: Shuri's oldest kura — kusu as Okinawa's treasure, rum and gin as its future.
okinawa:mizuho_shuzo.desc_en: Mizuho Shuzo, founded in 1848 in the Torihori quarter of Shuri — one of the royal Shuri Sanka — is the oldest surviving kura of the old capital. Under its creed that kusu is Okinawa's treasure, it also looks forward: the ONERUM rum from island sugarcane, the ORI-GiN craft gin, original yeast research, and Japan's pioneering awamori umeshu since 1971.
features_en: Rum, gin and yeast research beside the awamori

okinawa:okinawa_kenkyodo.tagline_en: All 46 awamori makers, one cooperative — and the 10-year Umi no Kuni.
okinawa:okinawa_kenkyodo.desc_en: The Okinawa Prefectural Distillery Cooperative was formed in September 1976 by all 46 of the prefecture's awamori makers. It buys members' awamori and ages it long for stable shipment beyond Okinawa — its Umi no Kuni, a ten-year kusu created for the 1987 Kaiho national games, is the flagship, with a fifteen-year edition above it.

okinawa:zuisen_shuzo.tagline_en: Named for the spring at Shuri castle's gate — 24 governor's prizes deep.
okinawa:zuisen_shuzo.desc_en: Zuisen Shuzo, founded in 1887 in Sakiyama — one of the royal brewing quarters of Shuri Sanka — takes its name from the Zuisen spring at Shuri Castle's Zuisenmon gate. It holds the record at the official awamori appraisal: 24 Okinawa governor's prizes as of 2020. Its labels still read Sakumoto no Sake, and the house shares family roots with Sakimoto Shuzo up the hill.
features_en: Named for the Shuri castle spring

御酒.specs_en: Awamori brewed with revived pre-war yeast

okinawa:tsuhako_shuzo.tagline_en: Taihei — great peace, bottled by hand since 1926.
okinawa:tsuhako_shuzo.desc_en: Tsuhako Shuzo, founded in 1898 in the Kakinohana quarter of Naha, has rested on one label since 1926: Taihei — great peace — its two circles standing for the earth and sun. Everything through bottling and labelling is done by hand, and on the second of each month the house holds its Taihei thanksgiving day, with limited bottles and time with the toji.
features_en: Monthly thanksgiving day at the kura

okinawa:kumesen_shuzo.tagline_en: Kumesen — one of awamori's great names, with an island whisky beside it.
okinawa:kumesen_shuzo.desc_en: Kumesen Shuzo, founded in 1952 in Naha and at its Nakaima home since 1986, brews one of Okinawa's defining awamori brands — from the everyday Kumesen to all-kusu gold and black editions — and now distils the OKINAWA ISLAND BLUE whisky as well.
features_en: One of Okinawa's defining awamori names

okinawa:miyasato_shuzo.tagline_en: Harusame — the phantom awamori that returned in 1997.
okinawa:miyasato_shuzo.desc_en: Miyasato Shuzosho, founded in 1946, named its awamori Harusame — spring rain — for hope and heaven's blessing. For some twenty years it sold only in bulk to other houses, never at retail, earning the name the phantom awamori; third-generation Toru Miyasato brought it back to shops in 1997. Aged koji gives its famously delicate touch.
features_en: The phantom awamori, retailed again from 1997

okinawa:uehara_shuzo.tagline_en: Shinsen — brewed again on the sacred spring of Itoman.
okinawa:uehara_shuzo.desc_en: Uehara Shuzo, founded in 1947, is Itoman's oldest awamori house. Its Shinsen — divine spring — thanks the Nbuga, the sacred spring behind the kura that has never run dry, and the house pioneered its own electronic technique for a mellow, deep pour. Silent from 2015, the stills came back to life in 2021; the premium bottling took gold at the 2022 awamori appraisal.

okinawa:masahiro_shuzo.tagline_en: A royal cook's family, brewing since 1883 — and Okinawa's first gin.
okinawa:masahiro_shuzo.desc_en: Masahiro Shuzo was founded in 1883 in Shuri by Shobun Higa, son of a cook to the royal court, under a royal brewing sanction. More than 140 years on — formerly Higa Shuzo — the Itoman house keeps black-koji tradition at the centre while pushing outward: it made Okinawa's first craft gin, Masahiro Okinawa Gin.

okinawa:kamiya_shuzo.tagline_en: Nanko — the light of the south, distilled by hand and steam.
okinawa:kamiya_shuzo.desc_en: Kamiya Shuzosho was founded in 1949 by Toshihiko Kamiya, naming its awamori Nanko — light of the south — as a beacon of hope in the post-war years. The house still refuses mechanisation, working by hand with its own steam-injection still, from the standard 30-degree to a 50-degree genshu.
features_en: Named the light of the south (1949)

okinawa:yoneshima_shuzo.tagline_en: Kume Island water, small batches, and blends worth remembering.
okinawa:yoneshima_shuzo.desc_en: Yoneshima Shuzo, founded in March 1948, brews on Kume Island — its founder fell for the island's abundant water and varied geology. A small hand-making house, it manages fermentation closely and blends awamori of different ages toward its stated ideal: easy to drink, deep to remember.

okinawa:kumejima_no_kumesen.tagline_en: The best-selling awamori in the world, from a hermit's legend.
okinawa:kumejima_no_kumesen.desc_en: Kumejima no Kumesen, founded in 1949, is the top-selling maker in the awamori industry. It brews with Kume Island's natural spring water, joining traditional fermentation to modern equipment on an island ringed entirely by coral reef. The name recalls the legend of a Kume Island hermit sage who poured sacred liquor for the islanders — and the company is distinct from Naha's Kumesen Shuzo.
features_en: Named for the island's hermit legend

okinawa:ikema_shuzo.tagline_en: Slow, cool fermentation on Miyako's mineral-hard water.
okinawa:ikema_shuzo.desc_en: Ikema Shuzo was founded in 1946, soon after the war, in the Nishihara district of Miyako Island. Its style rests on the island's mineral-rich hard water and slow, low-temperature fermentation under exacting control — bottled in labels from Zuiko to the cheerful Nikoniko Taro.

okinawa:okinohikari_shuzo.desc_en: Okinohikari Shuzo began in 1948 as the Koja Shuzosho, taking its present name in 1979. On Miyako Island it distils the flagship Okinohikari and companions such as Gekko no Hana.

okinawa:kikunotsuyu_shuzo.tagline_en: Kikunotsuyu — dew of the chrysanthemum, Miyako's standard-bearer.
okinawa:kikunotsuyu_shuzo.desc_en: Kikunotsuyu Shuzo, founded in 1928 as Nakao Shuzo and renamed in 1965, is Miyako Island's defining awamori house. The name comes from a Chinese tale — a sick mother healed by morning dew drunk from chrysanthemum petals — and the kura chases what it calls awamori's true deliciousness with craftsman stubbornness, from the daily 30-degree to the VIP Gold kusu.
features_en: Named from a Chinese filial tale
From daily pour to VIP Gold kusu

okinawa:taragawa.tagline_en: Ryukyu Ocho — kusu asleep in a natural cave, open to all comers.
okinawa:taragawa.desc_en: Taragawa, founded in 1948 in the Sunagawa district of Miyako, has held to hand technique for over seventy years. Its kusu — led by the famous Ryukyu Ocho (Royal Dynasty) — matures in the Uipya-Upusu natural cave cellar, which visitors may see without reservation, with a video of the brewing process shown at the kura.

okinawa:tokuyama_shuzo.tagline_en: Honen — a farmer's prayer for good harvest, on Irabu island water.
okinawa:tokuyama_shuzo.desc_en: Tokuyama Shuzo was founded in 1946 by Tomoaki Tokuyama of Irabu Island. A farmer himself, he named his awamori Honen — abundant harvest — as a prayer for the island's fields. Mineral-rich Irabu groundwater gives the spirit its bright, fresh aroma.

okinawa:miyanohana.tagline_en: A flower of the heart — awamori brewed largely by women.
okinawa:miyanohana.desc_en: Miyanohana, founded in 1948 on Irabu Island, takes its name from its founder's wish: to remain a flower blooming quietly in people's hearts, however small. Much of its team, from the president down, is women, and since 2006 the house has also brewed awamori from naturally farmed Japanese rice — no fertiliser, no pesticide.
features_en: The flower of the heart, since 1948

okinawa:chiyoizumi_shuzo.tagline_en: Chiyoizumi — a lost Miyako kura, revived drop by drop.
okinawa:chiyoizumi_shuzo.desc_en: Chiyoizumi Shuzosho, founded in 1948 in Miyako's Karimata district, was a small village kura beloved by its neighbours. It rested its stills in 2013 and closed in 2018 — the first awamori distillery to close since Okinawa's reversion — but part of its remaining spirit has been revived in limited bottlings through the Awamori Soko treasured-stock project.
features_en: Treasured stock revived in limited bottlings

okinawa:takamine_shuzo.tagline_en: Omoto — direct-flame stills two minutes from Kabira Bay.
okinawa:takamine_shuzo.desc_en: Takamine Shuzosho, founded in 1949, looks up at Mt. Omoto — Okinawa's highest peak — and out over the famous Kabira Bay. Everything is hand-made: koji rested two nights into old koji, and distillation over direct flame in a traditional ground kettle, on natural water of the Omoto range. Two minutes' walk from Kabira park; visitors welcome.
features_en: All handwork with direct-flame kettle stills

okinawa:tamanaha_shuzo.tagline_en: Yaeyama's oldest kura — Tama no Tsuyu, built to become kusu.
okinawa:tamanaha_shuzo.desc_en: Tamanaha Shuzosho, founded in 1912 as a branch of a Shuri house, is the oldest distillery in the Yaeyama islands, past its centenary in 2012. Nearly everything — koji, mash, distillation — is done by hand, with old koji and direct-kettle stills, brewing Tama no Tsuyu as awamori meant from the start to age into kusu.

okinawa:seifuku_shuzo.tagline_en: Innovator of Ishigaki — and reviver of the lost spirit IMUGE.
okinawa:seifuku_shuzo.desc_en: Seifuku Shuzo began in 1949 as the Kanna sakaya of Kenpu Kanna and his wife Fumie, renamed in 1992. It has innovated relentlessly — Okinawa's first printed bottle labels, the industry's first vacuum-distilled awamori — and revived IMUGE., the folk spirit of sweet potato and brown sugar lost for a century. Free tours daily at 14:00 (weekdays), no booking needed for small groups.
features_en: Revived the lost folk spirit IMUGE.

okinawa:ikehara_shuzo.tagline_en: Shirayuri — a divisive, beloved awamori saved by a grandson.
okinawa:ikehara_shuzo.desc_en: Ikehara Shuzo, founded in 1951 by Kokichi Ikehara in Ishigaki's Okawa quarter, brews in a red-tiled old house by unhurried tradition. Its Shirayuri (White Lily) is famous for a wild, singular flavour that drinkers either adore or argue about — and it took a top gold at a world competition in 2021. When closure loomed, grandson Yu Ikehara took over in 2013 and carried the kura on.

okinawa:yaesen_shuzo.tagline_en: Direct flame and long cask rest, on a hill over Ishigaki.
okinawa:yaesen_shuzo.desc_en: Yaesen Shuzo, founded in 1955 on a hill overlooking the Yaeyama ranges, takes its name from the island's natural springs. Direct-flame distillation meets long cask storage in a house that also makes habushu and fruit liqueurs — rich aroma, mellow sweetness. Shop open weekdays 9:00–17:30.
features_en: Habushu and liqueurs beside the awamori

okinawa:nakama_shuzo.tagline_en: Okinawa's smallest kura — one family, one label, made to order.
okinawa:nakama_shuzo.desc_en: Nakama Shuzosho, founded in 1948 by farmer Giichi Nakama in Ishigaki's Miyara district, is the smallest distillery in Okinawa. The family makes just one awamori — Miyanotsuru — and only as much as is ordered, steaming rice in a wooden kushichi and distilling in a direct-kettle still as they always have.

okinawa:hateruma_shuzo.tagline_en: Awanami — the phantom awamori of Japan's southernmost island.
okinawa:hateruma_shuzo.desc_en: Hateruma Shuzosho, founded in 1953 on Hateruma — Japan's southernmost inhabited island — is a five-person family kura of tiny production. About 95% of its Awanami never leaves the island, making the bottle a legend: the phantom awamori, its name woven from awamori's foam and Hateruma's waves.

okinawa:kokusen_awamori.tagline_en: Donan and its 60-degree hanazake, at Japan's westernmost edge.
okinawa:kokusen_awamori.desc_en: Kokusen Awamori was founded in 1958 by three partners on Yonaguni, Japan's westernmost island. The toji carries every step by hand from koji to bottling, with no artificial additives; Donan — 'Yonaguni' in the island tongue — runs from 25 degrees to the island's famous 60-degree hanazake, including a 17-year kusu of which only some 900 bottles exist.

okinawa:sakimoto_yonaguni_shuzo.tagline_en: Yonaguni's oldest kura, giving back with every recycled bottle.
okinawa:sakimoto_yonaguni_shuzo.desc_en: Sakimoto Shuzosho began in 1927 as the Kubura Shuzosho, founded by nineteen rice farmers, and became independent under its present name in 1971 — Yonaguni's oldest distillery. It keeps the 600-year awamori tradition with old-style ground-kettle stills and the island's 60-degree hanazake, bottles in recycled glass, and donates part of its sales to the island's emergency helicopter service. Tours in business hours.

okinawa:irinami_shuzo.tagline_en: Maifuna — the dutiful child, from Okinawa's youngest kura.
okinawa:irinami_shuzo.desc_en: Irinamihira Shuzo was founded in 1989 when Hironobu Irinamihira left Kokusen Awamori to start his own house — the newest distillery in Okinawa. Its Maifuna means a dutiful, praiseworthy child in the Yonaguni tongue, a wish that the drink bring joy; a 60-degree hanazake stands beside it. Reports suggest production is currently paused.

osaka:kotobuki_shuzo.tagline_en: Osaka's only local shochu, drawn from fresh sake lees each winter.
osaka:kotobuki_shuzo.desc_en: Kotobuki Shuzo, founded in 1822 in Takatsuki, makes the only shochu distilled in Osaka — its Kuninocho kasu-moromi shochu, drawn from fresh sake lees after pressing, produced only in winter. The house was also Osaka's first craft beer brewer.
features_en: Fresh sake-lees kasutori style, winter only

saga:munemasa.tagline_en: Nonnoko — 'sweet child' in Saga dialect, poured in a porcelain park.
saga:munemasa.desc_en: Munemasa Shuzo began distilling in 1985 in Imari and moved in 2002 into the Arita Porcelain Park, where it operates as a tourism kura. Its Nonnoko — Saga dialect for a darling child — is a barley shochu of 100% Saga two-row barley, with imo and long-aged rice versions, plus the sake Munemasa. Tours and tastings in the park.
features_en: Tourism kura in Arita Porcelain Park

saga:mitsutake.tagline_en: An invitation to the demon world, from a 1688 merchant street.
saga:mitsutake.desc_en: Mitsutake Shuzojo, founded in 1688 on the Hizen Hamashuku brewery street of Kashima, carries three centuries under its creed that making sake is making people. Its imo shochu Makai e no Izanai — Invitation to the Demon World — is black-koji brewed and atmospheric-distilled, and the Hizenya tourism kura welcomes travellers on the old street.
features_en: 300+ years on the Hizen Hamashuku street
Makai e no Izanai: black koji, atmospheric stills

saga:gochoda.tagline_en: Azumaichi — aiming to be the best in the East.
saga:gochoda.desc_en: Gochoda Shuzo, founded in 1922 in Ureshino, brews Azumaichi — a name that vows to become first in the East. An early mover in growing its own Yamada Nishiki in Saga, the house holds to local ingredients and sake the neighbourhood loves; its shochu carries the same discipline.

saga:baba.tagline_en: Nogomi — 370 koku a year under an owner-toji, since 1795.
saga:baba.desc_en: Baba Shuzojo, founded in 1795 in Kashima, brews about 370 koku a year under eighth-generation owner-toji Ichiro Baba. Seven years of work with local farmers brought Yamada Nishiki cultivation home to the neighbourhood, feeding its Nogomi label.
features_en: Local Yamada Nishiki after a 7-year project

saitama:asahara_shuzo.tagline_en: A distilling king among sake, fruit liqueurs and beer in Moroyama.
saitama:asahara_shuzo.desc_en: Asahara Shuzo, founded in 1882 in Moroyama, Saitama, brews the sake Biwa no Sasanami and Musashino, distils the honkaku shochu Joryu-O, and makes fruit liqueurs, wine and beer from local harvests. Tours and tastings at its Ogose Brewery shop.

shiga:ohta_shuzo.tagline_en: Organic Kintoki potatoes and brandy casks, by Ota Dokan's heirs.
shiga:ohta_shuzo.desc_en: Ohta Shuzo of Kusatsu, descended from Edo Castle's builder Ota Dokan, has brewed sake since 1874 and distilled honkaku shochu since 1918. Its imo shochu uses 100% pesticide-free Shiga-grown Kintoki sweet potatoes at atmospheric pressure, and its barley shochu rests long in brandy casks. Tours and a shop at the kura.

shimane:hikami.tagline_en: Soba shochu in the land of Izumo soba and tatara iron.
shimane:hikami.desc_en: Hikami Seishu has brewed for over 300 years in Okuizumo — myth country, home of tatara iron-making and of Izumo soba, one of Japan's three great buckwheat noodles. That heritage flows into its soba shochu, beside the sakes Shichikanba and Tamahagane.
features_en: Sakes named for a champion horse and tatara steel

七冠馬.specs_en: Sake — named for the seven-crown horse

tokushima:nisshin_shurui.tagline_en: Naruto Kintoki shochu — and now whisky — from the Taiko kura.
tokushima:nisshin_shurui.desc_en: Nisshin Shurui, Tokushima's full-range drinks maker, runs the Taiko Shuzojo and distils its imo shochu Naruto Kintoki Satomusume from 100% Tokushima-grown Naruto Kintoki sweet potatoes. In 2023 it added Japanese whisky at its Awano distillery.

tokyo:hachijo_kohatsu.tagline_en: Nasakeshima — GI Tokyo Island Shochu, sung in a Hachijo folk verse.
tokyo:hachijo_kohatsu.desc_en: Hachijo Kohatsu, founded in 1947 on Hachijojima, distils honkaku shochu certified under GI Tokyo Island Shochu. Its Nasakeshima — the isle of kindness — takes its name from a line of the island's Shome-bushi folk song, made with traditional technique and modern equipment. Tours by reservation.
features_en: Named from the island's folk song

tokyo:aogashima_shuzo.tagline_en: Aochu — ten toji, ten styles, on a far volcanic island.
tokyo:aogashima_shuzo.desc_en: Aogashima Shuzo makes Aochu, the phantom shochu of Aogashima — a volcanic speck far south of Tokyo. Home-grown sweet potatoes, Japanese barley and the island's own wild koji and yeasts are brewed donburi-style, and each of the ten toji ferments to their own hand: one island, many Aochus.
features_en: The phantom shochu of a remote island
Ten toji, each with their own style

tottori:matsui_shuzo.tagline_en: Japan's first low-temperature distillation, at the Kurayoshi Distillery.
tottori:matsui_shuzo.desc_en: Matsui Shuzo, founded in 1910, is Tottori's oldest incorporated brewer, running the Kurayoshi Distillery for shochu, whisky and gin. Its rice shochu Kurayoshi pioneered a patented vacuum still that distils at a low 35°C — a first in Japan. Distillery tours are offered.
features_en: Shochu, whisky and gin at Kurayoshi

wakayama:ozaki_shuzo.tagline_en: Kumano Suigun — rice shochu at the heart of the Kumano pilgrimage.
wakayama:ozaki_shuzo.desc_en: Ozaki Shuzo, founded around 1880 in Shingu, is the southernmost kura on Honshu, set at the heart of the World Heritage Kumano Sanzan shrines. Its rice shochu Kumano Suigun — named for the medieval Kumano navy — is vacuum-distilled from select rice, koji and ginjo lees on Kumano River subsoil water, and took second place in the national concours rice-shochu division.
features_en: At the Kumano World Heritage heart

yamagata:kinryu.tagline_en: Yamagata's only shochu specialist, born of nine sake kura.
yamagata:kinryu.desc_en: Kinryu, founded in 1950 in Sakata, is the only dedicated shochu maker in Yamagata, rooted in a fermentation company nine local sake breweries established to supply base alcohol. Its korui shochu So, launched in 1978, is the prefecture's household standard.

yamaguchi:nagayama_shuzo.tagline_en: Netaro — a folk-tale rice shochu born of a university partnership.
yamaguchi:nagayama_shuzo.desc_en: Nagayama Shuzo, founded in 1887 in the Asa district, spans sake, shochu and wine, with the Yamaguchi Winery on its grounds. Its rice shochu Netaro — named for the local folk tale of the boy who slept three years — was developed in the Showa 50s (late 1970s to early 1980s) with the prefectural technology centre and Yamaguchi University, fragrant and full of rice umami.
features_en: Sake, shochu and its own winery
Named from the Three-Year Netaro folk tale

yamaguchi:nagayama_honke.tagline_en: The Taka house of Ube — domaine brewing with a café in the kura.
yamaguchi:nagayama_honke.desc_en: Nagayama Honke Shuzojo, founded in 1895 in Ube, is known nationwide for its junmai sake Taka, brewed Burgundy-style — its own Yamada Nishiki paddies, mineral-rich water filtering off the Akiyoshidai plateau — with shochu in small volumes beside it. Its registered cultural-property buildings house the Futamatase Coffee café.
features_en: Domaine-style brewing with its own paddies
